translations.idiomatic: Father-zhao, son-mu, ancestral merit—only imperial sons and heaven's grandsons who received the mandate may be enshrined there.

sentences.zh: 但皇后祔廟，配食高宗，位號舊章，無宜稱帝。

translations.literal: But the empress enshrined in the temple, sharing sacrifice with Gaozong, by old title and statute ought not be called emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as consort sharing Gaozong's sacrifices, her old titles should not include "emperor."

sentences.zh: 今山陵日近，陞祔非遙，請申陳告之儀，因除『聖帝』之字，直題云『則天皇后武氏』。」

translations.literal: Now the imperial tomb day draws near and ascent to enshrinement is not distant; we ask to declare the announcement rite and remove the words "Holy Emperor," inscribing simply "Empress Zetian Wu."
translations.idiomatic: With her enshrinement near, we ask to perform the announcement rite, drop "Holy Emperor," and inscribe only "Empress Zetian Wu."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 時既另造義宗廟，將作大匠韋湊上疏曰：「臣聞王者制體，是曰規模；

translations.literal: At that time a separate Yizong Temple had been built; Master of Works Wei Cou submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that the king establishes the body—this is called the model;
translations.idiomatic: A separate Yizong Temple had been built; Master of Works Wei Cou wrote: "A king's institutions are his model;

sentences.zh: 規模之興，實資師古；

translations.literal: the rise of the model in fact relies on taking antiquity as teacher;
translations.idiomatic: and models must learn from antiquity;

sentences.zh: 師古之道，必也正名；

translations.literal: the Way of taking antiquity as teacher must rectify names;
translations.idiomatic: which requires correct names;

sentences.zh: 惟名與實，固當相副。

translations.literal: names and reality solidly ought to match each other.
translations.idiomatic: name and fact must agree.

sentences.zh: 其在宗廟，禮之大者，豈可失哉！

translations.literal: As for the ancestral temple, the greatest of rites—how can it be lost!
translations.idiomatic: In the ancestral temple, the greatest rite—how can it be neglected!

sentences.zh: 禮，祖有功而宗有德。

translations.literal: Ritual: the ancestor has merit, the clan lord has virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual holds that ancestors have merit and clan lords have virtue.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之廟，百代不毀。

translations.literal: The temples of ancestor and clan lord are not destroyed for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestor and clan-lord temples stand for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 故殷太甲曰太宗，太戊曰中宗，武丁曰高宗。

translations.literal: Thus Yin's Tai Jia was called Taizong, Tai Wu Zhongzong, Wu Ding Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's Tai Jia was styled Taizong, Tai Wu Zhongzong, and Wu Ding Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 周宗文王、武王。

translations.literal: Zhou honored King Wen and King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou honored Kings Wen and Wu.

sentences.zh: 漢則文帝為太宗，武帝為世宗。

translations.literal: Han made Emperor Wen Taizong and Emperor Wu Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Han styled Emperor Wen Taizong and Emperor Wu Shizong.

sentences.zh: 其後代有稱宗，皆以方制海內，德澤可宗，列于昭穆，期於不毀。

translations.literal: Afterward generations had those styled "zong," all because they regulated the realm within the four seas and their virtue and grace could be honored; ranked in zhao and mu, they were expected not to be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Later rulers styled "zong" when their virtue filled the realm and merited lasting place in the zhao-mu sequence.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之義，不亦大乎！

translations.literal: Is the meaning of "ancestor" and "zong" not also great!
translations.idiomatic: The weight of "ancestor" and "zong" is immense!

sentences.zh: 況孝敬皇帝位止東宮，未嘗南面，聖道誠冠于儲副，德教不被於寰瀛，立廟稱宗，恐非合體。

translations.literal: Moreover Emperor Xiaojing's position stopped at the Eastern Palace; he never faced south. His sagely Way indeed topped the heir, yet his moral teaching did not spread through the realm—establishing a temple and styling him zong, I fear, is not fitting the body of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaojing never ruled; though his virtue surpassed other heirs, his teaching did not reach the realm—calling him "zong" does not fit ritual.

sentences.zh: 況別起寢廟，不入昭穆，稽諸祀典，何義稱宗？

translations.literal: Moreover, if a separate sleeping temple is erected and he does not enter the zhao-mu sequence, then when this is checked against the sacrifice canon, by what principle can he be called zong?
translations.idiomatic: A separate shrine outside the zhao-mu line: how can it be called "zong" under the sacrifice canon?

sentences.zh: 而廟號義宗，稱之萬代。

translations.literal: Yet the temple name Yizong would be spoken for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the temple name Yizong would stand for ages.

sentences.zh: 以臣庸識，竊謂不可。

translations.literal: By your servant's shallow knowledge, I privately deem it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view it should not be done.

sentences.zh: 望更令有司詳定，務合於禮。」

translations.literal: I hope you will further order the relevant offices to examine in detail and ensure conformity with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will further order the relevant offices to examine in detail and ensure conformity with ritual."

sentences.zh: 於是太常請以本諡「孝敬」為廟稱。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Court of Imperial Sacrifices requested using the original posthumous title "Xiaojing" as the temple name.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices then proposed "Xiaojing," his posthumous title, as the temple name.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，玄宗將行幸東都，而太廟屋壞，乃奉七廟神主於太極殿。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, Xuanzong was about to travel to the eastern capital, but the Grand Temple buildings collapsed; he therefore moved the seven temples' tablets to Taiji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year's first month Xuanzong planned to visit the eastern capital; when the Grand Temple collapsed, he moved all seven tablets to Taiji Hall.

sentences.zh: 玄宗素服避正殿，輟朝三日，親謁神主於太極殿，而後發幸東都。

translations.literal: Xuanzong wore plain dress and avoided the main hall, halted court for three days, personally visited the tablets in Taiji Hall, and afterward set out for the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: He wore mourning dress, avoided the main hall, suspended court for three days, visited the tablets in Taiji Hall, then traveled east.

sentences.zh: 乃敕有司修太廟。

translations.literal: He then ordered the relevant offices to repair the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered repairs to the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 明年，廟成，玄宗還京，行親祔之禮。

translations.literal: The next year the temple was completed; Xuanzong returned to the capital and performed the rite of personal complementary enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: When the temple was finished the next year, he returned and performed the enshrinement rite in person.

sentences.zh: 時有司撰儀注，以祔祭之日車駕發宮中，玄宗謂宋璟、蘇頲曰：「祭必先齋，所以齊心也。

translations.literal: At the time, the offices drafted the ritual notes so that on the day of the enshrinement sacrifice the imperial carriage would depart from within the palace. Xuanzong said to Song Jing and Su Ting: "For sacrifice one must first fast, because this is how the mind is made uniform.
translations.idiomatic: When officials drafted the rite to have the emperor leave the palace on the enshrinement day, Xuanzong told Song Jing and Su Ting: "Sacrifice must be preceded by fasting, so the mind may be purified.

sentences.zh: 據儀注，祭之日發大明宮，又以質明行事，縱使侵星而發，猶是移辰方到，質明之禮，其可及乎？

translations.literal: According to the ritual notes, on the day of sacrifice we depart from Daming Palace, and the affair is carried out at daybreak. Even if we set out while encroaching on the stars, we would still arrive only after the hour had shifted; how could the daybreak rite be reached?
translations.idiomatic: The draft has us leave Daming Palace on the day itself and perform the rite at dawn. Even setting out before the stars fade, we would arrive only after the hour had passed; how could that be a dawn rite?

sentences.zh: 又朕不宿齋宮，即安正殿，情所不敢。

translations.literal: Moreover, for me not to lodge in the fasting palace but instead rest in the main hall is something my feelings do not dare.
translations.idiomatic: Nor do I dare avoid lodging in the fasting palace while resting in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 宜於廟所設齋宮，五日赴行宮宿齋，六日質明行事，庶合於禮。」

translations.literal: A fasting palace should be set up at the temple site. On the fifth day I should go to the temporary palace and lodge in fast, and on the sixth day carry out the rite at daybreak; this will perhaps accord with ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Set up a fasting palace at the temple. On the fifth day I will go there to fast overnight, and on the sixth perform the rite at dawn; only then may it accord with ritual."

sentences.zh: 璟等稱聖情深至，請即奉行。

translations.literal: Jing and the others praised the sagely feeling as deep and utmost, and requested that it be carried out at once.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing and the others praised the depth of his devotion and asked to implement the change at once.

sentences.zh: 詔有司改定儀注。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to revise the observances.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the rites revised.

sentences.zh: 六日，玄宗自齋宮步詣太廟，入自東門，就立位。

translations.literal: On the sixth day Xuanzong on foot went from the fasting palace to the Grand Temple, entered by the east gate, and took his standing position.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day he walked from the fasting palace to the Grand Temple, entered the east gate, and took his place.

sentences.zh: 樂奏九成，陞自阼階，行祼獻之禮。

translations.literal: Music played the Nine Completes; he ascended the eastern steps and performed the libation and offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Completes were played; he ascended the east steps and offered libation.

sentences.zh: 至睿宗室，俯伏鳴咽，侍臣莫不流涕。

translations.literal: Reaching Ruizong's chamber, he bowed prostrate and sobbed; attendants all wept.
translations.idiomatic: At Ruizong's chamber he prostrated himself and wept, and his attendants wept with him.

sentences.zh: 有河南府人孫平子詣闕上言：「中宗孝和皇帝既承大統，不合遷於別廟。」

translations.literal: A man of Henan prefecture, Sun Pingzi, came to the gate and stated: "Emperor Xiaojing of Zhongzong, having succeeded the great succession, ought not be moved to a separate temple.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Henan prefecture, Sun Pingzi, came to the gate and stated: "Emperor Xiaojing of Zhongzong, having succeeded the great succession, ought not be moved to a separate temple."

sentences.zh: 玄宗令宰相召平子與禮官對定可否，太常博士蘇獻等固執前議。

translations.literal: Xuanzong ordered the chancellor to summon Pingzi and the ritual officials to settle whether it was permissible; Court of Imperial Sacrifices Academician Su Xian and others stubbornly held to the prior discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong had the chancellor convene Pingzi and the ritualists; Su Xian and others clung to the earlier decision.

sentences.zh: 平子口辯，所引咸有經據，獻等不能屈。

translations.literal: Pingzi was sharp in debate; what he cited all had canonical basis—Xian and the rest could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzi argued forcefully with scriptural citations the ritualists could not refute.

sentences.zh: 時蘇頲知政事，以獻是其從祖之兄，頗党助之，平子之議竟不得行。

translations.literal: At that time Su Ting held government affairs; because Xian was his elder cousin's brother, he quite factionally aided him, and Pingzi's discussion in the end could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Su Ting, then in power, favored his cousin Su Xian, and Pingzi's proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 平子論竟不已，遂謫平子為康州都城尉，仍差使領送至任，不許東西。

translations.literal: Pingzi's discussion did not cease; he was then demoted to metropolitan magistrate of Kang prefecture, still sent under escort to his post, not permitted east or west.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingzi persisted, he was exiled as magistrate of Kang and escorted to his post under guard.

sentences.zh: 平子之任，尋卒。

translations.literal: Pingzi on taking up his post soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after arriving.

sentences.zh: 時雖貶平子，議者深以其言為是。

translations.literal: Though Pingzi was demoted at the time, discussants deeply took his words as correct.
translations.idiomatic: Despite his punishment, most officials thought him right.

sentences.zh: 至十年正月，下制曰：「朕聞王者乘時以設教，因事以制禮，沿革以從宜為本，取捨以適會為先。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, an edict was issued, saying: "I have heard that kings set teachings according to the times and make rites according to affairs; in continuation and reform, fittingness is the root, and in taking and discarding, meeting the occasion comes first.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year, an edict said: "I have heard that kings establish teaching according to the times and create rites according to events; reform and continuity must be based on what is fitting, and choices must suit the moment.

sentences.zh: 故損益之道有殊，質文之用斯異。

translations.literal: Therefore the ways of reduction and addition differ, and the uses of simplicity and ornament are thereby different.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the ways of adding and reducing differ, and simplicity and ornament are used differently.

sentences.zh: 且夫至德之謂孝，所以通乎神明；

translations.literal: Moreover, supreme virtue is called filial piety, by which one communicates with spirits and brightness;
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety is the highest virtue, the means of communicating with the spirits;

sentences.zh: 大事之謂祀，所以虔乎宗廟。

translations.literal: the great affair is called sacrifice, by which one is reverent in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: and sacrifice is the great affair, the way to show reverence in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 國家握紀命曆，重光累盛，四方由其繼明，七代可以觀德。

translations.literal: The state holds the order and commands the calendar; repeated brilliance and accumulated prosperity have followed, the four quarters depend on its continuing light, and through seven generations virtue can be observed.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty holds the mandate and calendar; its brightness and prosperity have continued, the four quarters depend on its light, and seven generations reveal its virtue.

sentences.zh: 朕嗣守丕業，祗奉睿圖，聿懷昭事，罔不恤祀。

translations.literal: I have inherited and guarded the great enterprise, reverently upheld the sagely plan, and constantly kept in mind clear service; there is no sacrifice I do not attend to.
translations.idiomatic: In inheriting this great enterprise and reverently upholding the ancestral plan, I keep solemn service in mind and neglect no sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 嘗覽古典，詢諸舊制，遠則夏、殷事異，近則漢、晉道殊，雖禮文之不一，固嚴敬之無二。

translations.literal: I have examined ancient canons and inquired into old systems. Far back, Xia and Yin affairs differed; nearer, Han and Jin ways differed. Though ritual forms are not the same, solemn reverence is certainly not two.
translations.idiomatic: I have reviewed ancient texts and old institutions: Xia and Yin differed in antiquity, Han and Jin in later times. Ritual forms vary, but solemn reverence does not.

sentences.zh: 朕以為立愛自親始，教人睦也；

translations.literal: I think that establishing love begins from kin, teaching people harmony;
translations.idiomatic: I believe love begins with kinship and teaches people harmony;

sentences.zh: 立敬自長始，教人順也。

translations.literal: establishing reverence begins from elders, teaching people obedience.
translations.idiomatic: reverence begins with elders and teaches people obedience.

sentences.zh: 是知朕率於禮，緣於情，或教以道存，或禮從時變，將因宜以創制，豈沿古而限今。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that I follow ritual and proceed from feeling: sometimes teaching is preserved through the Way, sometimes ritual changes with the times. I am about to create a system according to what is fitting, not follow antiquity and thereby limit the present.
translations.idiomatic: Thus I follow ritual while giving due place to feeling: teaching may preserve the Way, and ritual may change with the time. I will establish a system suited to the occasion, not bind the present by antiquity.

sentences.zh: 況恩以降殺而疏，廟以遷毀而廢。

translations.literal: How much more when affection becomes distant through graded reduction, and temples are abolished through removal and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Affection grows distant through graded reduction, and temples disappear through removal and destruction.

sentences.zh: 雖式瞻古訓，禮則不違；

translations.literal: Although we respectfully look to ancient instructions and do not violate ritual;
translations.idiomatic: Even while observing the ancient instructions and not violating ritual;

sentences.zh: 而永言孝思，情所未足。

translations.literal: yet when I continually speak of filial thought, feeling is not yet satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: my filial feeling remains unsatisfied.

sentences.zh: 享嘗則止，豈愛崇而禮備；

translations.literal: If offerings and seasonal sacrifices merely stop, how can love be honored and ritual complete;
translations.idiomatic: If regular offerings merely cease, how can love be honored and ritual made complete;

sentences.zh: 有禱而祭，非德盛而流永。

translations.literal: if there is sacrifice only when there is prayer, this is not virtue flourishing and flowing forever.
translations.idiomatic: and if sacrifice is made only for petitions, virtue cannot flourish and endure.

sentences.zh: 其祧室宜列為正室，使親而不盡，遠而不禰，廟以貌存，宗猶尊立。

translations.literal: The tiao chambers should be arrayed as proper chambers, causing kinship not to be exhausted, the distant not to be treated as the father, the temple to remain by its form, and the zong still to stand honored.
translations.idiomatic: The removed chambers should be made regular chambers, preserving kinship without confusing distant ancestors with the immediate father, keeping the temple form intact and the honored line standing.

sentences.zh: 俾四時式薦，不間於毀主；

translations.literal: Let the four seasons present offerings according to rule, without interruption for removed tablets;
translations.idiomatic: Let seasonal offerings continue by rule, without interruption for tablets otherwise removed;

sentences.zh: 百代靡遷，匪惟於始廟。

translations.literal: let there be no moving for a hundred generations, not only in the founder's temple.
translations.idiomatic: and let tablets remain unmoved for a hundred generations, not only in the founder's temple.

sentences.zh: 所謂變以合禮，動而得中，嚴配之典克崇，肅雍之美茲在。

translations.literal: This is what is called changing in order to accord with ritual, acting and obtaining the mean; the canon of solemn enshrinement can be exalted, and the beauty of reverent harmony lies here.
translations.idiomatic: This is change that accords with ritual and action that reaches the mean; it exalts solemn enshrinement and preserves reverent harmony.

sentences.zh: 又兄弟繼及，古有明文。

translations.literal: Moreover, for brothers succeeding one another, antiquity has clear texts.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient texts also clearly address succession among brothers.

sentences.zh: 今中宗神主，猶居別處，詳求故實，當寧不安，移就正廟，用章大典。

translations.literal: Now Zhongzong's spirit tablet still resides in a separate place. When I examine precedent in detail, I am uneasy at court. It should be moved to the proper temple, thereby displaying the great canon.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong's tablet still remains elsewhere. Examining the precedents, I am uneasy on the throne; it should be moved into the main temple to display the great canon.

sentences.zh: 仍創立九室，宜令所司擇日啟告移遷。」

translations.literal: Also create and establish nine chambers; the responsible offices should be ordered to choose a day, announce it, and carry out the transfer."
translations.idiomatic: Establish nine chambers, and order the offices to choose a day, announce the move, and transfer the tablets."

sentences.zh: 十一年春，玄宗還京師，下制曰：「崇建宗廟，禮之大者；

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year, Xuanzong returned to the capital and issued an edict, saying: "Honoring and building the ancestral temple is the great matter of ritual;
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year, Xuanzong returned to the capital and issued an edict: "Building up the ancestral temple is one of ritual's greatest matters;

sentences.zh: 聿追孝饗，德莫至焉。

translations.literal: pursuing filial offerings, no virtue is more utmost than this.
translations.idiomatic: nothing in virtue is greater than carrying out filial offerings.

sentences.zh: 今宗以立尊，親無遷序，永惟嚴配，致用蠲潔，棟宇式崇，祼奠斯授。

translations.literal: Now the zong is used to establish honor, kin have no sequence of removal, and I ever think of solemn enshrinement; service must be pure, the buildings are reverently exalted, and libations and offerings are thereby presented.
translations.idiomatic: Now honored temples have been established and kin are no longer ordered for removal. I constantly think on solemn enshrinement: service must be pure, the halls honored, and libations and offerings presented.

sentences.zh: 顧茲薄德，獲承禋祀，不躬不親，曷展誠敬？

translations.literal: Looking to my slight virtue, I have received the sacrifices; if I do not personally and intimately attend, how can I display sincere reverence?
translations.idiomatic: With my slight virtue I have inherited these sacrifices; if I do not attend them personally, how can I show sincere reverence?

sentences.zh: 宜用八月十九日祗見九室。」

translations.literal: It is proper to use the nineteenth day of the eighth month to reverently visit the nine chambers."
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth day of the eighth month I shall reverently visit the nine chambers."

sentences.zh: 於是追尊宣皇帝為獻祖，復列於正室，光皇帝為懿祖，並還中宗神主於太廟。

translations.literal: Thereupon Emperor Xuan was posthumously honored as Xianzu and again arrayed in a proper chamber; Emperor Guang was made Yizu; and Zhongzong's spirit tablet was also returned to the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was then honored as Xianzu and restored to a main chamber, Emperor Guang as Yizu, and Zhongzong's tablet was returned to the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 及將親祔，會雨而止。

translations.literal: When he was about to perform personal complementary enshrinement, rain stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Rain halted the planned personal enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 乃令所司行事。

translations.literal: He then ordered the relevant offices to perform the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He had the offices carry out the rite instead.

sentences.zh: 其京師中宗舊廟，便毀拆之。

translations.literal: The old Zhongzong temple in the capital was then torn down.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong's former capital temple was demolished.

sentences.zh: 東都舊廟，始移孝敬神主祔焉。

translations.literal: In the eastern capital's old temple, the tablet of Xiaojing was first moved to complementary enshrinement there.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojing's tablet was first enshrined in the eastern capital's old temple.

sentences.zh: 其從善裏孝敬舊廟，亦令毀拆。

translations.literal: The old Xiaojing temple in Congshan Lane was also ordered demolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiaojing shrine in Congshan Lane was also torn down.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，玄宗又特令遷肅明皇后神主祔于睿宗之室，仍以舊儀坤廟為肅明觀。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Xuanzong again specially ordered the tablet of Empress Suming moved to share sacrifice in Ruizong's chamber; the old Yikun Temple was still made the Suming Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-one he moved Suming's tablet to Ruizong's chamber and converted Yikun Temple into Suming Abbey.

sentences.zh: 大曆十四年十月，代宗神主將祔，禮儀使顏真卿以元皇帝代數已遠，准禮合祧，請遷於西夾室。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourteenth year of Dali, as Daizong's spirit tablet was about to be enshrined, Ritual Commissioner Yan Zhenqing, because Emperor Yuan was already distant in generations and according to ritual should be removed, requested moving him to the western side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Dali 14, tenth month: when Daizong's tablet was to be installed, Yan Zhenqing argued that Emperor Yuan was too remote by generation and should be moved to the western side chamber.

sentences.zh: 其奏議曰：《王制》：「天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。」

translations.literal: His memorial stated: The 《Wang System》 says, "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao and three mu, and with the temple of the Grand Ancestor they make seven."
translations.idiomatic: His memorial cited the 《Wang System》: "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao, three mu, plus the Grand Ancestor."

sentences.zh: 又《禮器》云：有以多為貴者，天子七廟。」

translations.literal: The 《Ritual Vessels》 also says, "In cases where more is honored, the Son of Heaven has seven temples."
translations.idiomatic: The 《Ritual Vessels》 likewise says that when number marks honor, the Son of Heaven has seven temples.

sentences.zh: 又《伊尹》曰：「七代之廟，可以觀德。」

translations.literal: The 《Yi Yin》 also says, "From the temples of seven generations, one can observe virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The 《Yi Yin》 adds: "Seven generations of temples let one observe virtue."

sentences.zh: 此經典之明證也。

translations.literal: These are clear proofs from the classics.
translations.idiomatic: These classics give clear evidence.

sentences.zh: 七廟之外，則曰：「去祧為壇，去壇為墠」。

translations.literal: Outside the seven temples, it says: "When removed from the tiao shrine, make an altar; when removed from the altar, make an open sacrifice ground."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the seven temples, the rule is: "removed from the tiao shrine, it becomes an altar; removed from the altar, it becomes an open ground."

sentences.zh: 故歷代儒者，制迭毀之禮，皆親盡宜毀。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucian scholars of successive ages, in establishing the rite of successive removal, all held that when kinship was exhausted, removal was proper.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Confucian scholars through the ages set the rite of successive removal: once kinship is exhausted, removal is proper.

sentences.zh: 伏以太宗文皇帝，七代之祖；

translations.literal: I submit that Taizong, Emperor Wen, is the ancestor of the seventh generation;
translations.idiomatic: I submit: Taizong, Emperor Wen, is seven generations back;

sentences.zh: 高祖神堯皇帝，國朝首祚，萬葉所承；

translations.literal: Gaozu, Emperor Shenyao, began the dynasty's fortune, inherited through ten thousand generations;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, Emperor Shenyao, founded the dynasty's fortune, carried through all later generations;

sentences.zh: 太祖景皇帝，受命于天，始封于唐，元本皆在不毀之典。

translations.literal: Taizu, Emperor Jing, received the mandate from Heaven and was first enfeoffed in Tang; these foundations all fall under the canon of non-removal.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, Emperor Jing, received Heaven's mandate and first held Tang; these founding roots all belong among those never removed.

sentences.zh: 代祖元皇帝，地非開統，親在七廟之外。

translations.literal: Daizu, Emperor Yuan, did not occupy the place of opening the line, and in kinship stands outside the seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: Daizu, Emperor Yuan, did not found the line and by kinship falls outside the seven temples.

sentences.zh: 代宗皇帝升祔有日，元皇帝神主，禮合祧遷。

translations.literal: The day for Emperor Daizong's elevation and enshrinement has arrived; according to ritual, Emperor Yuan's spirit tablet should be removed and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: With Daizong's enshrinement at hand, ritual requires Emperor Yuan's tablet to be removed.

sentences.zh: 或議者以祖宗之名，難於迭毀。

translations.literal: Some discussants, because of the names "ancestor" and "zong," considered successive removal difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that titles such as "ancestor" and "zong" made removal difficult.

sentences.zh: 昔漢朝近古，不敢以私滅公，故前漢十二帝，為祖宗者四而已。

translations.literal: Formerly the Han court was close to antiquity and did not dare let private feeling extinguish public principle; therefore, of the twelve Former Han emperors, only four were made Zu or Zong.
translations.idiomatic: The Han, still near antiquity, did not let private feeling override public rule; of twelve Former Han emperors, only four were named Zu or Zong.

sentences.zh: 至後漢漸違經意，子孫以推美為先。

translations.literal: By Later Han, they gradually departed from the meaning of the classics, and descendants put the advancement of praise first.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han gradually strayed from the classics, with descendants intent on praise.

sentences.zh: 自光武已下，皆有廟號，則祖宗之名，莫不建也。

translations.literal: From Guangwu downward, all had temple names, so the names Zu and Zong were all established.
translations.idiomatic: From Guangwu on, every emperor had a temple name; Zu and Zong titles became universal.

sentences.zh: 安帝信讒，害大臣，廢太子，及崩，無上宗之奏，後自建武以來無毀者，因以陵號稱宗。

translations.literal: Emperor An believed slander, harmed great ministers, and deposed the heir apparent. When he died, there was no memorial to elevate him as Zong; later, because none had been removed since Jianwu, he was called Zong by his mausoleum title.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An trusted slander, killed ministers, and deposed the heir; no one memorialized to honor him as Zong, but since no temple had been removed since Jianwu, he was styled Zong by mausoleum name.

sentences.zh: 至桓帝失德，尚有宗號。

translations.literal: When it came to Emperor Huan, who lost virtue, he still had the title Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Even Emperor Huan, despite his loss of virtue, still received a Zong title.

sentences.zh: 故初平中，左中郎蔡邕以和帝以下，功德無殊，而有過差，不應為宗。

translations.literal: Thus in the Chuping era, Left Palace Attendant Cai Yong held that from Emperor He downward, their achievements and virtue were not exceptional, while they had faults and errors, and they should not be Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in Chuping, Cai Yong argued that from Emperor He down, their merit and virtue were undistinguished and their faults real, so they should not be Zong.

sentences.zh: 余非宗者，追尊三代，皆奏毀之。

translations.literal: For the rest who were not Zong, including the three generations posthumously honored, he memorialized that they all be removed.
translations.idiomatic: For the remaining non-Zong temples, including three posthumously honored generations, he memorialized removal.

sentences.zh: 是知祖有功，宗有德，存至公之義，非其人不居，蓋三代立禮之本也。

translations.literal: From this we know that Zu is for merit and Zong is for virtue; preserving the principle of utmost public fairness, one who is not the proper person does not occupy the place. This is probably the foundation of ritual established by the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zu means merit and Zong means virtue; public principle requires that only the proper person hold the place. This was the ritual foundation of the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 自東漢已來，則此道衰矣。

translations.literal: Since Eastern Han, this way has declined.
translations.idiomatic: Since Eastern Han, that principle declined.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝自稱烈祖，論者以為逆自稱祖宗。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei called himself Liezu, and critics considered this a perverse self-assumption of an ancestral title.
translations.idiomatic: Ming of Wei called himself Liezu; critics saw this as arrogating an ancestral title to himself.

sentences.zh: 故近代此名悉為廟號，未有子孫踐祚而不祖宗先王者。

translations.literal: Therefore in recent ages these names all became temple names, and there has been no descendant who ascended the throne and did not make former kings Zu or Zong.
translations.idiomatic: In recent ages these titles all became temple names; no descendant took the throne without making earlier rulers Zu or Zong.

sentences.zh: 以此明之，則不得獨據兩字而為不合祧遷之證。

translations.literal: Viewed in this light, one cannot rely solely on the two characters as proof that removal and transfer are improper.
translations.idiomatic: So the two titles alone cannot prove that removal is ritually improper.

sentences.zh: 假令傳祚百代，豈可上崇百代以為孝乎？

translations.literal: If the dynastic fortune were transmitted for a hundred generations, could one exalt a hundred generations above and call that filial piety?
translations.idiomatic: If the throne passed through a hundred generations, could exalting all hundred be called filial piety?

sentences.zh: 請依三昭三穆之義，永為通典。

translations.literal: I request that we follow the meaning of the three zhao and three mu and make it a permanent general rule.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the three zhao and three mu principle become the permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 寶應二年，升祔玄宗、肅宗，則獻祖、懿祖已從迭毀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoying, when Xuanzong and Suzong were elevated and enshrined, Xianzu and Yizu had already undergone successive removal.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying 2: when Xuanzong and Suzong were enshrined, Xianzu and Yizu had already been removed in turn.

sentences.zh: 伏以代宗睿文孝皇帝卒哭而祔，則合上遷一室。

translations.literal: We note Emperor Daizong the Filial, at the end of wailing and enshrinement, ought to move up one chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong's enshrinement after mourning requires shifting one chamber upward.

sentences.zh: 元皇帝代數已遠，其神主准禮當祧，至禘祫之時，然後享祀。

translations.literal: The Yuan Emperor's generations are already distant; his tablet per ritual should be removed; at the di and xia rites he would then be offered sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan Emperor is too remote; his tablet should be removed and honored only at the great di and xia sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 於是祧元皇帝于西夾室，祔代宗神主焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Yuan Emperor was removed to the western side chamber and Daizong's tablet was enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan Emperor was moved to the western side chamber and Daizong was enshrined.

sentences.zh: 永貞元年十一月，德宗神主將祔，禮儀使杜黃裳與禮官王涇等請遷高宗神主於西夾室。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Yongzhen, as Emperor Dezong's tablet was about to be enshrined, Ritual Commissioner Du Huangchang and ritual officials Wang Jing and others requested moving Gaozong's tablet to the western side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhen 1, eleventh month: when Dezong's tablet was to be installed, Du Huangchang and Wang Jing proposed moving Gaozong to the western side chamber.

sentences.zh: 其議曰：「自漢、魏已降，沿革不同。

translations.literal: Their discussion stated: "From Han and Wei down, institutions differ.
translations.idiomatic: They argued: "Since Han and Wei, practice has varied.

sentences.zh: 古者祖有功，宗有德，皆不毀之名也。

translations.literal: In antiquity the ancestor had merit and the clan lord had virtue—both are names not destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity held that meritorious ancestors and virtuous clan lords were never removed.

sentences.zh: 自東漢、魏、晉，迄于陳、隋，漸違經意，子孫以推美為先，光武已下，皆有祖宗之號。

translations.literal: From Eastern Han, Wei, and Jin through Chen and Sui, they gradually departed from the classic intent; descendants took extolling beauty as foremost; from Guangwu down all had ancestor-and-clan-lord designations.
translations.idiomatic: From Eastern Han through Sui, courts increasingly praised forebears for flattery; after Guangwu nearly every emperor received "ancestor" or "zong" titles.

sentences.zh: 故至於迭毀親盡，禮亦迭遷，國家九廟之尊，皆法周制。

translations.literal: Thus when successive removal exhausted kin, ritual also shifted in turn; the state's nine temples' honor all follow Zhou's system.
translations.idiomatic: As kinship lapsed, tablets were removed in turn; the nine-temple system follows Zhou.

sentences.zh: 伏以太祖景皇帝受命于天，始封元本，德同周之后稷也。

translations.literal: We note the Great Ancestor Emperor Jing received the mandate from Heaven, first enfeoffed the primal root—his virtue equals Zhou's Hou Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Great Ancestor Jing received Heaven's mandate and founded the line, like Zhou's Hou Ji.

sentences.zh: 高祖神堯皇帝國朝首祚，萬葉所承，德同周之文王也。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor Emperor Shen Yao was the dynasty's first reign, the myriad leaves' inheritance—his virtue equals Zhou's King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: High Ancestor Shen Yao began the dynasty, like Zhou's King Wen.

sentences.zh: 太宗文皇帝應天靖亂，垂統立極，德同周武王也。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong the Cultural responded to Heaven, quelled disorder, and handed down the succession—his virtue equals Zhou's King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong pacified the realm and established the succession, like Zhou's King Wu.

sentences.zh: 周人郊后稷而祖文王、宗武王，聖唐郊景皇帝、祖高祖而宗太宗，皆在不遷之典。

translations.literal: Zhou in the suburbs honored Hou Ji and in the temple took King Wen as ancestor and King Wu as clan lord; sagely Tang in the suburbs honors Emperor Jing and in the temple takes the High Ancestor as ancestor and Taizong as clan lord—all in the canon of non-removal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sacrificed to Hou Ji and honored Wen and Wu in the temple; Tang sacrifices to Jing, with Shen Yao as ancestor and Taizong as zong—all never removed.

sentences.zh: 高宗皇帝今在三昭三穆之外，謂之親盡，新主入廟，禮合迭遷，藏於從西第一夾室，每至禘祫之月，合食如常。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong is now outside the three zhao and three mu—called kin exhausted; with a new tablet entering the temple, ritual requires successive removal, stored in the first side chamber from the west; each di and xia month he is jointly offered as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong is now outside the three zhao and three mu—called kin exhausted; with a new tablet entering the temple, ritual requires successive removal, stored in the first side chamber from the west; each di and xia month he is jointly offered as usual."

sentences.zh: 於是祧高宗神主於西夾室，祔德宗神主焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gaozong's tablet was removed to the western side chamber and Dezong's tablet was enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong was moved to the western side chamber and Dezong was enshrined.

sentences.zh: 元和元年七月，順宗神主將祔，有司疑於遷毀，太常博士王涇建議曰：禮經「祖有功，宗有德」，皆不毀之名也。

translations.literal: In Yuanhe 1, seventh month, when Shunzong's spirit tablet was about to be enshrined, the offices were uncertain about removal and destruction, and Grand Ritual Erudite Wang Jing proposed: the ritual classics say, "Ancestors have merit, and zong have virtue"; these are both names for those not destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 1, seventh month, as Shunzong's tablet was to be enshrined, officials were uncertain which tablet should be removed. Grand Ritual Erudite Wang Jing argued that the ritual classics say, "Ancestors have merit, and zong have virtue," both names for tablets never removed.

sentences.zh: 惟三代行之。

translations.literal: Only the Three Dynasties practiced this.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Three Dynasties truly followed this rule.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏已降，雖曰祖宗，親盡則遷，無功亦毀，不得行古之道也。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei downward, although they were called zu and zong, when kinship was exhausted they were moved, and if they had no merit they were also destroyed; they could not practice the ancient way.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei onward, even rulers called zu or zong were moved when kinship ended, and those without merit were removed; the ancient standard was no longer kept.

sentences.zh: 昔夏后氏十五代，祖顓頊而宗禹。

translations.literal: Formerly the Xiahou clan had fifteen generations, made Zhuanxu the ancestor, and made Yu the zong.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia rulers counted fifteen generations, honoring Zhuanxu as ancestor and Yu as zong.

sentences.zh: 殷人十七代，祖契而宗湯。

translations.literal: The Yin people had seventeen generations, made Xie the ancestor, and made Tang the zong.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin counted seventeen generations, honoring Xie as ancestor and Tang as zong.

sentences.zh: 周人三十六王，以后稷為太祖，祖文王而宗武王。

translations.literal: The Zhou people had thirty-six kings, made Hou Ji the Grand Ancestor, made King Wen the ancestor, and made King Wu the zong.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou had thirty-six kings, with Hou Ji as Grand Ancestor, King Wen as ancestor, and King Wu as zong.

sentences.zh: 聖唐德厚流廣，遠法殷、周，奉景皇帝為太祖，祖高祖而宗太宗，皆在百代不遷之典。

translations.literal: The sagely Tang has deep virtue and broad transmission, distantly models itself on Yin and Zhou, serves Emperor Jing as Grand Ancestor, makes Gaozu the ancestor and Taizong the zong; all are within the canon of not being moved for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Our Tang, rich in virtue and broad in succession, follows Yin and Zhou: Emperor Jing is Grand Ancestor, Gaozu is ancestor, and Taizong is zong, all within the canon of tablets never moved.

sentences.zh: 故代宗升祔，遷代祖也；

translations.literal: Thus when Daizong was enshrined, Daizu was moved;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Daizu was moved when Daizong was enshrined;

sentences.zh: 德宗升祔，遷高宗也。

translations.literal: when Dezong was enshrined, Gaozong was moved.
translations.idiomatic: and Gaozong was moved when Dezong was enshrined.

sentences.zh: 今順宗升祔，中宗在三昭三穆之外，謂之親盡，遷於太廟夾室，禮則然矣。

translations.literal: Now that Shunzong is being enshrined, Zhongzong is outside the three zhao and three mu; this is called kinship exhausted. Moving him to a side chamber of the Grand Temple is what ritual requires.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Shunzong is being enshrined, Zhongzong falls outside the three zhao and three mu. His kinship line is exhausted, so ritual requires moving him to a Grand Temple side chamber.

sentences.zh: 或諫者以則天太后革命，中宗復而興之，不在遷藏之例，臣竊未諭也。

translations.literal: Some remonstrators think that Empress Zetian changed the dynasty and Zhongzong restored and revived it, so he is not within the precedent of removal and storage; I privately do not understand this.
translations.idiomatic: Some object that because Empress Zetian changed the dynasty and Zhongzong restored it, he should not be treated as a tablet to be moved and stored. I do not understand this argument.

sentences.zh: 昔者高宗晏駕，中宗奉遺詔，自儲副而陟元后。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Gaozong died, Zhongzong received the testamentary edict and rose from crown prince to sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong died, Zhongzong followed the testamentary edict and ascended from heir apparent to sovereign.

sentences.zh: 則天太后臨朝，廢為盧陵王。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Zetian governed at court, she deposed him as Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Zetian took court power, she deposed him as Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 聖曆元年，太后詔復立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In Shengli 1, the empress dowager issued an edict restoring and installing him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengli 1 she restored him as crown prince by edict.

sentences.zh: 屬太后聖壽延長，御下日久，奸臣擅命，紊其紀度。

translations.literal: Because the empress dowager's sacred longevity was prolonged and she ruled those below for many days, wicked ministers monopolized commands and disturbed the order.
translations.idiomatic: Because the empress dowager lived and ruled for so long, wicked ministers seized authority and disrupted the order of government.

sentences.zh: 敬暉、桓彥範等五臣，俱唐舊臣，匡輔王室，翊中宗而承大統。

translations.literal: Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, and the other five ministers were all old Tang ministers; they rectified and assisted the royal house, supported Zhongzong, and had him inherit the great line.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, and the other five ministers were old Tang servants who supported the royal house and helped Zhongzong resume the succession.

sentences.zh: 此乃子繼父業，是中宗得之而且失之；

translations.literal: This was the son continuing the father's enterprise: Zhongzong obtained it and then lost it;
translations.idiomatic: This was a son inheriting his father's work: Zhongzong gained the throne and then lost it;

sentences.zh: 母授子位，是中宗失之而復得之。

translations.literal: and the mother giving the son the position: Zhongzong lost it and then obtained it again.
translations.idiomatic: then his mother returned the position to her son, so Zhongzong regained what he had lost.

sentences.zh: 二十年間，再為皇太子，復踐皇帝位，失之在己，得之在己，可謂革命中興之義殊也。

translations.literal: Within twenty years, he twice became crown prince and again trod the imperial position. Losing it lay in himself, obtaining it lay in himself; this can be called different from the meaning of dynastic change and restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Over twenty years he twice became crown prince and returned to the imperial throne. The loss and recovery both belonged to his own line, so this differs from true dynastic restoration.

sentences.zh: 又以周、漢之例推之，幽王為犬戎所滅，平王東遷，周不以平王為中興不遷之廟，其例一也。

translations.literal: Moreover, extending from the examples of Zhou and Han: King You was destroyed by the Quanrong and King Ping moved east, yet Zhou did not make King Ping an unmoved temple of restoration; this is the first example.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou example is first: after King You was destroyed by the Quanrong and King Ping moved east, Zhou did not make King Ping an unmoved restoration temple.

sentences.zh: 漢呂后專權，產、祿秉政，文帝自代邸而立之，漢不以文帝為中興不遷之廟，其例二也。

translations.literal: In Han, Empress Lü monopolized power, Chan and Lu held government, and Emperor Wen was installed from his residence in Dai, yet Han did not make Emperor Wen an unmoved temple of restoration; this is the second example.
translations.idiomatic: The Han example is second: when Empress Lü monopolized power and Lü Chan and Lü Lu governed, Emperor Wen came from Dai to take the throne, yet Han did not give him an unmoved restoration temple.

sentences.zh: 霍光輔宣帝，再盛基業，而不以宣帝為不遷之廟，其例三也。

translations.literal: Huo Guang assisted Emperor Xuan and again made the foundation flourish, yet they did not make Emperor Xuan an unmoved temple; this is the third example.
translations.idiomatic: The third example is Huo Guang's support of Emperor Xuan, which renewed the dynasty but still did not make Xuan an unmoved temple.

sentences.zh: 伏以中宗孝和皇帝，于聖上為六代伯祖，尊非正統，廟亦親盡。

translations.literal: I submit that Emperor Xiaohe Zhongzong is, to the Sage Above, an elder uncle ancestor of the sixth generation; his rank is not in the direct line, and his temple has also exhausted kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong, Emperor Xiaohe, is a sixth-generation collateral ancestor to the present emperor, not in the direct line, and his temple kinship is exhausted.

sentences.zh: 爰及周、漢故事，是與中興功德之主不同，奉遷夾室，固無疑也。

translations.literal: Extending to the precedents of Zhou and Han, this is different from a lord of restoration merit and virtue; respectfully moving him to the side chamber is certainly without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: By the precedents of Zhou and Han, he is not a restoration ruler of enduring merit. There is no doubt that his tablet should be moved to the side chamber.

sentences.zh: 是月二十四日，禮儀使杜黃裳奏曰：「順宗皇帝神主已升祔太廟，告祧之後，即合遞遷。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day of that month Director of Ritual Du Huangchang memorialized: "Emperor Shunzong's tablet has already ascended to complementary enshrinement in the Grand Temple; after announcing removal, it should shift in turn.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth Du Huangchang reported: "Shunzong is already in the Grand Temple; after the removal announcement his predecessors should shift.

sentences.zh: 中宗皇帝神主，今在三昭三穆之外，准禮合遷於太廟從西第一夾室，每至禘祫之日，合食如常。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong's tablet is now outside the three zhao and three mu; per ritual he should be moved to the Grand Temple's first side chamber from the west; on each di and xia day he is jointly offered as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong's tablet is now outside the three zhao and three mu; per ritual he should be moved to the Grand Temple's first side chamber from the west; on each di and xia day he is jointly offered as usual."

sentences.zh: 於是祧中宗神主於西夾室，祔順宗神主焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhongzong's tablet was removed to the western side chamber and Shunzong's tablet was enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was moved to the western side chamber and Shunzong was enshrined.

sentences.zh: 有司先是以山陵將畢，議遷廟之禮。

translations.literal: The relevant offices had earlier, because the imperial tomb was nearing completion, discussed the rite of temple removal.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as the imperial tomb neared completion, the offices had debated temple removal.

sentences.zh: 有司以中宗為中興之君，當百代不遷之位。

translations.literal: The relevant offices took Zhongzong as a restoration ruler and entitled to the position not removed for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: They argued Zhongzong was a restoration emperor who should never be removed.

sentences.zh: 宰臣召史官蔣武問之，武對曰：「中宗以弘道元年于高宗柩前即位，時春秋已壯矣。

translations.literal: The chancellor summoned the historiographer Jiang Wu and asked him about it. Wu replied: "Zhongzong took the throne before Gaozong's coffin in the first year of Hongdao; at the time, he was already mature in years.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor asked historiographer Jiang Wu, who replied: "Zhongzong took the throne before Gaozong's coffin in Hongdao 1, when already mature.

sentences.zh: 及母后篡奪，神器潛移。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager usurped, the sacred vessel shifted in secret.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager seized power, the throne was lost.

sentences.zh: 其後賴張柬之等同謀，國祚再復。

translations.literal: Afterward, relying on Zhang Jianzhi and others in common plot, the imperial fortune was twice restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Jianzhi and his allies restored him—twice.

sentences.zh: 此蓋同於反正，恐不得號為中興之君。

translations.literal: This is roughly like a return to correctness; I fear he may not be styled a restoration ruler.
translations.idiomatic: That resembles mere restoration, not the "restoration emperor" of ritual theory.

sentences.zh: 凡非我失之，自我復之，謂之中興，漢光武、晉元帝是也。

translations.literal: What is not lost by oneself but restored by oneself is called restoration—Han Guangwu and Jin Yuandi are cases.
translations.idiomatic: True restoration means regaining what one lost oneself, as with Guangwu or Jin's Yuandi.

sentences.zh: 自我失之，因人復之，晉孝惠、孝安是也。

translations.literal: What is lost by oneself but restored through others—Jin's Emperor Hui and Emperor An are cases.
translations.idiomatic: Losing the throne and recovering it through others, as with Jin's Hui and An, is different.

sentences.zh: 今中宗于惠、安二帝事同，即不可為不遷之主也。」

translations.literal: Now Zhongzong's affair is the same as the two emperors Hui and An; he cannot be a ruler not removed.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhongzong's affair is the same as the two emperors Hui and An; he cannot be a ruler not removed."

sentences.zh: 有司又云：「五王有再安社稷之功，今若遷中宗廟，則五王永絕配享之例。」

translations.literal: The relevant offices also said: "The Five Kings had the achievement of twice settling the altars of soil and grain; if Zhongzong's temple is now moved, the Five Kings will forever cut off the precedent of shared sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: The offices added: "Moving Zhongzong would end the Five Kings' shared sacrifice forever."

sentences.zh: 武曰：凡配享功臣，每至禘祫年方合食太廟，居常即無享禮。

translations.literal: Wu said: Generally meritorious ministers sharing sacrifice only at di and xia years jointly eat in the Grand Temple; in ordinary times there is no offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: Wu replied: Merit-sharing ministers are fed in the Grand Temple only at di and xia; otherwise they receive no regular offerings.

sentences.zh: 今遷中宗神主，而禘祫之年，毀廟之主並陳於太廟，此同五王配食，與前時如一也。」

translations.literal: Now moving Zhongzong's tablet—in di and xia years, destroyed-temple rulers are all arrayed in the Grand Temple; this is the same as the Five Kings' shared sacrifice, as before.
translations.idiomatic: Moving Zhongzong still leaves the Five Kings honored at di and xia when removed rulers are assembled—no change for them.

sentences.zh: 有司不能答。

translations.literal: The relevant offices could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The offices had no reply.

sentences.zh: 十五年四月，禮部侍郎李建奏上大行皇帝諡曰聖神章武孝皇帝，廟號憲宗。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year, Vice Minister of Rites Li Jian memorialized the late emperor's posthumous title as Emperor Sheng Shen Zhang Wu Xiao and temple name Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year Li Jian proposed the posthumous title Sheng Shen Zhang Wu Xiao and temple name Xianzong for the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 先是，河南節度使李夷簡上議曰：「王者祖有功，宗有德。

translations.literal: Earlier, Military Commissioner of Henan Li Yijian had submitted a discussion, saying: "Kings take as ancestor those with merit and as clan lord those with virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Yijian of Henan had argued: "Kings honor meritorious ancestors and virtuous clan lords.

sentences.zh: 大行皇帝戡翦寇逆，累有武功，廟號合稱祖。

translations.literal: The late emperor cut down rebels and bandits and repeatedly had military achievements; the temple name ought to be styled zu.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor suppressed rebellion with repeated military success; his temple name should be zu, not zong.

sentences.zh: 陛下正當決在宸斷，無信齷齪書生也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should decide this at the imperial throne; do not trust pedantic bookish scholars."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should decide this at the imperial throne; do not trust pedantic bookish scholars."

sentences.zh: 遂詔下公卿與禮官議其可否。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was sent down to the dukes and ministers and ritual officials to debate whether it was permissible.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered the chief ministers and ritual officers to debate the proposal.

sentences.zh: 太常博士王彥威奏議：「大行廟號，不宜稱祖，宜稱宗。」

translations.literal: Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wang Yanwei memorialized: "The temple name of the late emperor should not be called Zu; it should be called Zong."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Wang Yanwei argued: "The late emperor's temple name should be Zong, not Zu."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 其月，禮部奏：「准貞觀故事，遷廟之主，藏於夾室西壁南北三間。

translations.literal: That month the Ministry of Rites memorialized: "According to the Zhenguan precedent, removed temple tablets are stored in the three north–south chambers on the west wall of the side chambers.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Ministry of Rites memorialized: "According to the Zhenguan precedent, removed temple tablets are stored in the three north–south chambers on the west wall of the side chambers.

sentences.zh: 第一間代祖室，第二間高宗室，第三間中宗室。

translations.literal: The first chamber was the chamber of the dynastic founder; the second, the chamber of Emperor Gaozong; the third, the chamber of Emperor Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: The first room was for the dynastic founder, the second for Gaozong, the third for Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 伏以山陵日近，睿宗皇帝祧遷有期，夾室西壁三室外，無置室處。

translations.literal: We note that the imperial tomb day draws near and Emperor Ruizong's removal is due; beyond the three chambers on the west wall of the side chambers there is no place to set a chamber.
translations.idiomatic: With Ruizong's enshrinement imminent, no room remained on the west side-chamber wall beyond the three existing chambers.

sentences.zh: 准《江都集禮》：『古者遷廟之主，藏於太室北壁之中。』

translations.literal: According to the 《Jiangdu Collected Rites》: "In antiquity, removed temple tablets were stored within the north wall of the Grand Chamber."
translations.idiomatic: The 《Jiangdu Collected Rites》 say ancient removed tablets were kept in the Grand Chamber's north wall.

sentences.zh: 今請於夾室北壁，以西為上，置睿宗皇帝神主石室。」

translations.literal: Now we request on the north wall of the side chambers, taking west as superior, to place the stone chamber for Emperor Ruizong's spirit tablet."
translations.idiomatic: Now we request on the north wall of the side chambers, taking west as superior, to place the stone chamber for Emperor Ruizong's spirit tablet."

sentences.zh: 制從之。

translations.literal: The decree followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年正月，禮儀使奏：「謹按《周禮》：『天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。』

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Changqing, the Ritual Commissioner memorialized: "We respectfully examine the 《Zhou Rites》: 'The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao and three mu, and with the temple of the Grand Ancestor they make seven.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing 4, first month: the ritual commissioner cited the 《Zhou Rites》 on the Son of Heaven's seven temples: three zhao, three mu, plus the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 《荀卿子》曰：『有天下者祭七代，有一國者祭五代。』

translations.literal: The 《Xunzi》 says: "He who possesses All-under-Heaven sacrifices to seven generations; he who possesses one state sacrifices to five generations."
translations.idiomatic: The 《Xunzi》 says a ruler of the realm sacrifices to seven generations, a feudal lord to five.

sentences.zh: 則知天子上祭七廟，典籍通規。

translations.literal: Thus we know that the Son of Heaven ascends to sacrifice at seven temples—this is the universal rule in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: So seven ancestral temples for the Son of Heaven is the classical norm.

sentences.zh: 祖功宗德，不在其數。

translations.literal: Ancestral merit and dynastic virtue are not counted in that number.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious ancestors and dynastic founders lie outside that count.

sentences.zh: 國朝九廟之制，法周之文。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's system of nine ancestral temples follows the Zhou pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's nine-shrine system follows the Zhou model.

sentences.zh: 太祖景皇帝，始為唐公，肇基天命，義同周之后稷。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing, who first became Duke of Tang and inaugurated the Mandate, is analogous to Hou Ji of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing, first Duke of Tang and founder of the Mandate, matches Zhou's Hou Ji.

sentences.zh: 高祖神堯皇帝，創業經始，代隋為唐，義同周之文王。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong the Divine Yao, who founded the enterprise and replaced Sui with Tang, is analogous to King Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong the Divine Yao, who founded the dynasty, matches King Wen.

sentences.zh: 太宗文皇帝，神武應期，造有區夏，義同周之武王。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong the Cultured, martial and responsive to the age, who made the realm, is analogous to King Wu of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong the Cultured, who pacified the realm, matches King Wu.

sentences.zh: 其下三昭三穆，謂之親廟，四時常饗，自如禮文。

translations.literal: Below them the three zhao and three mu are called the intimate temples; seasonal offerings follow the ritual text as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Below them the three zhao and three mu are the "intimate" shrines with regular seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 今以新主入廟，玄宗明皇帝在三昭三穆之外，是親盡之祖，雖有功德，禮合祧遷，禘祫之歲，則從合食。」

translations.literal: Now with a new tablet entering the temple, Emperor Xuanzong the Brilliant lies outside the three zhao and three mu; he is an ancestor whose line of descent is exhausted. Though he has merit and virtue, ritual requires removal; in the years of di and xia he joins the combined feast."
translations.idiomatic: Now with a new tablet entering the temple, Emperor Xuanzong the Brilliant lies outside the three zhao and three mu; he is an ancestor whose line of descent is exhausted. Though he has merit and virtue, ritual requires removal; in the years of di and xia he joins the combined feast."

sentences.zh: 制從之，

translations.literal: The decree followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 開成五年，禮儀使奏：「謹按天子七廟，祖功宗德，不在其中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaicheng, the Ritual Commissioner memorialized: "We respectfully note that the Son of Heaven's seven temples do not include meritorious ancestors and virtuous founders.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaicheng, the Ritual Commissioner memorialized: "We respectfully note that the Son of Heaven's seven temples do not include meritorious ancestors and virtuous founders.

sentences.zh: 國朝制度，太廟九室。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's institution: the Grand Temple has nine chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Under dynastic practice the Grand Temple has nine chambers.

sentences.zh: 伏以太祖景皇帝受封于唐，高祖、太宗，創業受命，有功之主，百代不遷。

translations.literal: We note that the Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing received enfeoffment in Tang; Gaozong and Taizong founded the enterprise and received the Mandate—meritorious rulers are not removed for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Jing, Gaozong, and Taizong—founders with merit—are never removed.

sentences.zh: 今文宗元聖昭獻皇帝升祔有時，代宗睿文孝武皇帝是親盡之祖，禮合祧遷，每至禘祫，合食如常。」

translations.literal: Now Emperor Wenzong the Sagely Illustrious is due to ascend; Emperor Daizong the Sagely Cultured and Martial is an exhausted-line ancestor whom ritual requires to remove; at each di and xia he joins the combined feast as usual."
translations.idiomatic: Now Emperor Wenzong the Sagely Illustrious is due to ascend; Emperor Daizong the Sagely Cultured and Martial is an exhausted-line ancestor whom ritual requires to remove; at each di and xia he joins the combined feast as usual."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 會昌元年六月，制曰：「朕近因載誕之日，展承顏之敬，太皇太后謂朕曰：『天子之孝，莫大於丕承；人倫之義，莫大于嗣續。穆宗睿聖文惠孝皇帝厭代已久，星霜屢遷，禰宮曠合食之禮，惟帝深濡露之感。宣懿皇太后，長慶之際，德冠後宮，夙表沙麓之祥，實茂河洲之範。先朝恩禮之厚，中壺莫偕。況誕我聖君，纘承昌運，已協華於先帝，方延祚於後昆。思廣貽謀，庶弘博愛，爰從舊典，以慰孝思。當以宣懿皇太后祔太廟穆宗睿聖文惠孝皇帝之室。率是彝訓，其敬承之。』朕祇奉慈旨，載深感咽。宜令宣示中外，咸使聞知。」會昌六年五月，禮儀使奏：武宗昭肅皇帝祔廟，併合祧遷者。伏以自敬宗、文宗、武宗兄弟相及，已歷三朝。昭穆之位，與承前不同。所可疑者，其事有四：一者，兄弟昭穆同位，不相為後；二者，已祧之主，復入舊廟；三者，廟數有限，無後之主，則宜出置別廟；四者，兄弟既不相為後，昭為父道，穆為子道，則昭穆同班，不合異位。據《春秋》「文公二年，躋僖公」。何休云：躋，升也，謂西上也。惠公與莊公當同南面西上，隱、桓與閔、僖當同北面西上。」孔穎達亦引此義釋經。又賀循云：「殷之盤庚，不序陽甲；漢之光武，上繼元帝。」晉元帝、簡文，皆用此義毀之，蓋以昭穆位同，不可兼毀二廟故也。《尚書》曰：「七代之廟，可以觀德。」且殷家兄弟相及，有至四帝不及祖禰，何容更言七代，於理無矣。二者，今已兄弟相及，同為一代，矯前之失，則合復祔代宗神主於太廟。或疑已祧之主，不合更入太廟者。按晉代元、明之時，已遷豫章、潁川矣，及簡文即位，乃元帝之子，故復豫章、潁川二神主於廟。又國朝中宗已祔太廟，至開元四年，乃出置別廟，至十年，置九廟，而中宗神主復祔太廟。則已遷復入，亦可無疑。三者，廟有定數，無後之主，出置別廟者。按魏、晉之初多同廟，蓋取上古清廟一宮，尊遠神祗之義。自後晉武所立之廟，雖云七主，而實六代，蓋景、文同廟故也。又按魯立姜嫄、文王之廟，不計昭穆，以尊尚功德也。晉元帝上繼武帝，而惠、懷、湣三帝，時賀循等諸儒議，以為別立廟，親遠義疏，都邑遷異，於理無嫌也。今以文宗棄代才六七年，武宗甫邇復土，遽移別廟，不齒祖宗，在於有司，非所宜議。四者，添置廟之室。按《禮論》，晉太常賀循云：「廟以容主為限，無拘常數。」故晉武帝時，廟有七主六代。至元帝、明帝，廟皆十室。及成、康、穆三帝，皆至十一室。自後雖遷故祔新，大抵以七代為准，而不限室數。伏以江左大儒，通賾睹奧，事有明據，固可施行。今若不行是議，更以迭毀為制，則當上不及高曾未盡之親，下有忍臣子恩義之道。今備討古今，參校經史，上請復代宗神主於太廟，以存高曾之親。下以敬宗、文宗、武宗同為一代，於太廟東間添置兩室，定為九代十一室之制，以全臣子恩敬之義，庶協大順之宜，得變禮之正，折古今之紛互，立群疑之杓指。俾因心廣孝，永燭於皇明；昭德事神，無虧於聖代。敕曰：「宗廟事重，實資參詳。宜令尚書省、兩省、御史臺四品以上官、大理卿、京兆尹等集議以聞。」尚書左丞鄭涯等奏議曰：「夫禮經垂則，莫重于嚴配，必參損益之道，則合典禮之文。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Huichang, an edict said: "Recently, on the day of my birth anniversary, when I displayed the reverence of attending upon her countenance, the Grand Empress Dowager told me: 'Of the filial duty of the Son of Heaven, nothing is greater than grandly continuing the succession; of the obligations of human relations, nothing is greater than heirs continuing the line. Emperor Muzong, the Sagely, Cultured, Benevolent, and Filial, has long since left the age, and years and seasons have repeatedly passed. His paternal temple chamber lacks the rite of sharing food, and only the emperor deeply feels the grief of dew and frost. Empress Dowager Xuanyi, in the Changqing era, surpassed the rear palace in virtue, early displayed the auspicious sign of Shalu, and truly flourished in the model of Hezhou. In the former reign the thickness of grace and ritual had no equal within the inner palace. How much more, since she gave birth to our sage ruler and continued the prosperous fortune, already sharing splendor with the former emperor and about to extend blessing to later descendants. Thinking to broaden the plans left to posterity and hoping to enlarge universal love, follow the old canon and so comfort filial thoughts. Empress Dowager Xuanyi should be attached in the Great Temple to the chamber of Emperor Muzong, the Sagely, Cultured, Benevolent, and Filial. Take this constant instruction as your model, and reverently carry it out.' I have respectfully received the compassionate command and am deeply moved and choked with feeling. Let it be proclaimed inside and outside, so that all may hear and know it." In the fifth month of the sixth year of Huichang, the Commissioner of Ritual Protocol memorialized that when Emperor Wuzong, the Illustrious and Solemn, was attached to the temple, the tablets to be removed should also be considered together. Respectfully, since Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong succeeded one another as brothers, three reigns have already passed. Their zhao and mu positions differ from the former pattern. There are four matters that may be doubted. First, brothers occupy the same zhao-mu position and do not become successors to one another. Second, a tablet already removed may again enter the old temple. Third, the number of temple chambers is limited, and a tablet without a successor should be taken out and placed in a separate temple. Fourth, since brothers do not become successors to one another, zhao is the way of the father and mu is the way of the son; if zhao and mu are in the same rank, they should not occupy different positions. According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, "In the second year of Duke Wen, Duke Xi was raised." He Xiu says, "Raised means promoted, meaning westward precedence. Duke Hui and Duke Zhuang should face south together, with the westward place highest; Duke Yin, Duke Huan, Duke Min, and Duke Xi should face north together, with the westward place highest." Kong Yingda also cited this meaning in explaining the classic. He Xun also said, "Pangeng of Yin did not arrange Yangjia in sequence; Guangwu of Han continued upward from Emperor Yuan." Emperor Yuan and Emperor Jianwen of Jin both used this principle in removing temples, probably because when zhao and mu positions are the same, two temples cannot both be removed. The Book of Documents says, "In the temples of seven generations, virtue may be observed." Moreover, in the Yin house brothers succeeded one another, at times with four emperors not reaching grandfather or father; how could one then further speak of seven generations? In principle this is impossible. Second, now that brothers have succeeded one another and together form one generation, correcting the former error means that Emperor Daizong's spirit tablet should again be attached in the Great Temple. Some may doubt that a tablet already removed should again enter the Great Temple. But in the Jin, during the times of Yuan and Ming, Yuzhang and Yingchuan had already been moved out; when Jianwen ascended the throne, he was Emperor Yuan's son, and so the two spirit tablets of Yuzhang and Yingchuan were restored to the temple. Also, in our dynasty Zhongzong had already been attached in the Great Temple; in the fourth year of Kaiyuan he was taken out and placed in a separate temple, but in the tenth year, when nine temples were established, Zhongzong's spirit tablet was again attached in the Great Temple. Thus there should also be no doubt about restoring a tablet that has already been moved. Third, as for the temple having a fixed number and placing a tablet without a successor in a separate temple: at the beginning of Wei and Jin many shared the same temple, probably taking the ancient meaning of one clear temple hall and honoring remote deities. Afterward, in the temple established by Emperor Wu of Jin, though it was called seven tablets, it was in fact six generations, because Jing and Wen shared one temple. Again, Lu established temples for Jiang Yuan and King Wen without counting zhao and mu, in order to honor merit and virtue. Emperor Yuan of Jin continued upward from Emperor Wu, while for the three emperors Hui, Huai, and Min, the scholars He Xun and others debated at the time and considered that separate temples should be established; with kinship distant and obligation sparse, and with capital city and territory changed, there was no impropriety in principle. Now Wenzong has left the age only six or seven years ago, and Wuzong has only just recently returned to the earth; suddenly moving them to separate temples and not ranking them among the ancestors is not something the responsible offices should discuss. Fourth, as to adding temple chambers: according to the Discussion of Rites, He Xun, Chamberlain for Ceremonials of Jin, said, "A temple is limited by its capacity to hold tablets and is not bound to a constant number." Therefore, in Emperor Wu of Jin's time, the temple had seven tablets and six generations. By the time of Emperors Yuan and Ming, the temples both had ten chambers. With Emperors Cheng, Kang, and Mu, they all reached eleven chambers. Afterward, although old tablets were moved and new ones attached, in general seven generations served as the standard, but the number of chambers was not limited. Respectfully, the great scholars south of the Yangzi understood subtlety and saw what was profound; since the matter has clear evidence, it may certainly be carried out. If this proposal is not now carried out, and alternating removal is instead made the rule, then above it will fail to reach the not-yet-exhausted kinship of great-grandfather and grandfather, and below there will be the way of a minister and son enduring the loss of grace and obligation. Having now fully examined ancient and recent cases and compared classics and histories, we request above that Emperor Daizong's spirit tablet be restored to the Great Temple, preserving the kinship of great-grandfather and grandfather. Below, with Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong together forming one generation, add two chambers in the eastern bay of the Great Temple and fix the system as nine generations and eleven chambers, in order to complete the obligation of grace and reverence owed by ministers and sons. This will nearly accord with the propriety of great obedience, obtain the correctness of adapting ritual, settle the disputes of ancient and recent times, and establish a handle and guide for all doubts. It will let filial piety broaden from the heart and forever shine in imperial brightness; it will manifest virtue in serving the spirits and leave no deficiency in the sage age. An edict said: "The matter of the ancestral temple is weighty and truly requires joint deliberation. Let the Department of State Affairs, the two Secretariats, officials of the fourth rank and above in the Censorate, the Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, the Intendant of Jingzhao, and others assemble and debate it for report." Vice Minister of the Left in the Department of State Affairs Zheng Ya and others memorialized in deliberation, saying: "The ritual classics hand down standards, and nothing is weightier than solemnly pairing the ancestors. One must consult the principle of adding and reducing; then it accords with the texts of canonical ritual.
