sentences.zh: 況有明徵，是資折衷。

translations.literal: Moreover there are clear proofs—this supports a balanced decision.
translations.idiomatic: Clear precedents supported a balanced ruling.

sentences.zh: 伏自敬宗、文宗、武宗三朝嗣位，皆以兄弟，考之前代，理有顯據。

translations.literal: We note that Emperors Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong succeeded in turn, all as brothers; examining earlier ages, reason gives plain evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong had succeeded as brothers—a pattern with clear precedent in earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 今謹詳禮院所奏，並上稽古文，旁摭史氏，協於通變，允謂得宜。

translations.literal: Now we respectfully examine in detail what the Ritual Institute memorialized, and above trace ancient texts and on the side gather historians; it harmonizes with timely change and may be called fitting.
translations.idiomatic: They reviewed the Ritual Institute's proposal against classics and history and found it a timely, fitting compromise.

sentences.zh: 臣等商議，請依禮官所議。」

translations.literal: Your subjects deliberated and request following what the ritual officers proposed."
translations.idiomatic: Your subjects deliberated and request following what the ritual officers proposed."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 大中三年十一月，制追尊憲宗、順宗諡號，事下有司。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Dazhong, an edict posthumously elevated the honorific titles of Xianzong and Shunzong, and the matter was sent down to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong 3, eleventh month: an edict raised Xianzong's and Shunzong's posthumous titles and referred implementation to the offices concerned.

sentences.zh: 太常博士李稠奏請別造憲宗、順宗神主，改題新諡。

translations.literal: Erudite Li Chou memorialized requesting separately to make new spirit tablets for Xianzong and Shunzong and change the inscriptions to the new honorifics.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Li Chou asked to carve new tablets for Xianzong and Shunzong bearing the new titles.

sentences.zh: 上疑其事，詔都省集議。

translations.literal: The emperor doubted the matter and ordered the Department of State Affairs to assemble for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doubted this and ordered a joint deliberation at the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 右司郎中楊發、都官員外郎劉彥模等奏：「考尋故事，無別造神主改題之例。」

translations.literal: Director of the Right Bureau Yang Fa, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Liu Yanmo, and others memorialized: "When we examine past precedents, there is no example of separately making spirit tablets and changing their inscriptions."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fa and Liu Yanmo memorialized: "There is no precedent for new tablets and retitled inscriptions."

sentences.zh: 事在《楊發傳》。

translations.literal: The matter is in the 《Biography of Yang Fa》.
translations.idiomatic: The full debate is recorded in the 《Biography of Yang Fa》.

sentences.zh: 時宰臣奏：「改造改題，並無所據，酌情順理，題則為宜。

translations.literal: At the time the chief ministers memorialized: "Remaking and retitling both lack authority; weighing sentiment and reason, retitling is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the chief ministers memorialized: "Remaking and retitling both lack authority; weighing sentiment and reason, retitling is fitting.

sentences.zh: 況今士族之家，通行此例，雖尊卑有異，而情理則同。

translations.literal: Moreover among gentry families today this practice is common; though noble and base differ, sentiment and reason are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry families commonly retitled tablets; rank differed, but the principle was the same.

sentences.zh: 望就神主改題，則為通允。」

translations.literal: We hope to retitle on the existing spirit tablets—then it will be broadly acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: We hope to retitle on the existing spirit tablets—then it will be broadly acceptable."

sentences.zh: 依之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 黃巢犯長安，僖宗避狄於成都府。

translations.literal: Huang Chao attacked Chang'an; Emperor Xizong avoided the Di barbarians at Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao took Chang'an, Xizong fled to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 中和元年夏四月，有司請享太祖已下十一室，詔公卿議其儀。

translations.literal: In the summer, fourth month, of the first year of Zhonghe, the responsible offices requested offering to the eleven chambers from the Grand Ancestor down; an edict ordered the dukes and ministers to debate the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe 1, summer, fourth month: officers sought to sacrifice at all eleven chambers from the Grand Ancestor down, and the court ordered debate on the rite.

sentences.zh: 太常卿牛叢與儒者同議其事。

translations.literal: Director of Imperial Sacrifices Niu Cong deliberated the matter together with Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Director Niu Cong and the ritual scholars debated the matter.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「王者巡狩，以遷廟主行。

translations.literal: Someone said: "When the king tours the regions, he takes the removed temple tablets on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said: "When the king tours the regions, he takes the removed temple tablets on the journey.

sentences.zh: 如無遷廟之主，則祝奉幣帛皮珪告于祖禰，遂奉以出，載于齋車，每舍奠焉。

translations.literal: If there are no removed temple tablets, the invoker presents silks, fabrics, pelts, and jade scepters to announce to the ancestors, then bears them out, loads them on the fasting carriage, and offers at each lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Without removed tablets, invokers would announce to the ancestors with silks and jade, then carry the tablets in the fasting carriage, offering at each stop.

sentences.zh: 今非巡狩，是失守宗廟。

translations.literal: Now this is not a tour—it is the loss of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: This was not a royal tour but the loss of the capital temple.

sentences.zh: 夫失守宗廟，則當罷宗廟之事。」

translations.literal: When the ancestral temple is lost, ancestral temple affairs should be suspended."
translations.idiomatic: When the ancestral temple is lost, ancestral temple affairs should be suspended."

sentences.zh: 叢疑之。

translations.literal: Cong doubted this.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Cong was uncertain.

sentences.zh: 將作監王儉、太子賓客李匡乂、虞部員外郎袁皓建議同異。

translations.literal: Director of Palace Construction Wang Jian, Palace Mentor Li Kuangyi, and Vice Director of the Ministry of Works Yuan Hao proposed differing plans.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, Li Kuangyi, and Yuan Hao offered conflicting proposals.

sentences.zh: 及左丞崔厚為太常卿，遂議立行廟。

translations.literal: When Left Vice Director Cui Hou became Director of Imperial Sacrifices, they then resolved to establish a traveling temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Hou became director, they resolved to set up a traveling temple.

sentences.zh: 以玄宗幸蜀時道宮玄元殿之前，架幄幕為十一室。

translations.literal: At the time when Emperor Xuanzong visited Shu, before the Daoist palace Hall of the Mysterious Origin, they erected curtain frames as eleven chambers.
translations.idiomatic: They had once framed eleven curtained chambers before the Hall of the Mysterious Origin when Xuanzong fled to Shu.

sentences.zh: 又無神主，題神版位而行事。

translations.literal: Again there were no spirit tablets; they inscribed spirit boards and conducted the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Without tablets they used inscribed boards and performed the rites.

sentences.zh: 達禮者非之，以為止之可也。

translations.literal: Those versed in ritual criticized this, holding that stopping would be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual experts criticized the practice and said it should simply stop.

sentences.zh: 明年，乃特造神主以祔行廟。

translations.literal: The next year they specially made spirit tablets to enshrine in the traveling temple.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they specially carved tablets for the traveling temple.

sentences.zh: 光啟元年十二月二十五日，僖宗再幸寶雞。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month of the first year of Guangqi, Emperor Xizong again visited Baoji.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi 1, twelfth month, twenty-fifth day: Xizong again reached Baoji.

sentences.zh: 其太廟十一室並祧廟八室及孝明太皇太后等別廟三室等神主，緣室法物，宗正寺官屬奉之隨駕鄠縣，為賊所劫，神主、法物皆遺失。

translations.literal: The spirit tablets of the Grand Temple's eleven chambers, the eight chambers of the removed temple, and the three separate temples of the Filial and Bright Grand Empress Dowager and others, together with ritual objects for the chambers, were escorted by officials of the Court of the Imperial Clan following the imperial progress to Hao County; bandits robbed them and the spirit tablets and ritual objects were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven Grand Temple tablets, eight removed-shrine tablets, three empress-dowager shrine tablets, and ritual gear—escorted by the clan court to Hao County—were looted and lost.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，車駕自興元還京，以宮室未備，權駐鳳翔。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year the imperial carriage returned to the capital from Xingyuan; because the palaces were not ready, it temporarily lodged at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, second month: the court returned from Xingyuan but lodged at Fengxiang while palaces were rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 禮院奏：「皇帝還宮，先謁太廟。

translations.literal: The Ritual Institute memorialized: "When the emperor returns to the palace, he first visits the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Institute memorialized: "When the emperor returns to the palace, he first visits the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 今宗廟焚毀，神主失墜，請准禮例修奉者。」

translations.literal: Now the ancestral temple is burned and destroyed and the spirit tablets are lost; we request following ritual precedent to restore and maintain them."
translations.idiomatic: Now the ancestral temple is burned and destroyed and the spirit tablets are lost; we request following ritual precedent to restore and maintain them."

sentences.zh: 禮院獻議曰：「按《春秋》：『新宮災，三日哭。』

translations.literal: The Ritual Institute presented a deliberation, saying: "According to the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》: 'When the new palace suffered fire, there was weeping for three days.
translations.idiomatic: The institute cited the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》: when the new palace burned, three days of mourning were prescribed.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：『新宮，宣公廟也。

translations.literal: The 《Commentary》 says: 'The new palace was Duke Xuan's temple.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Commentary》 explains the "new palace" was Duke Xuan's temple.

sentences.zh: 三日哭，禮也。』

translations.literal: Weeping for three days is ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Three days of weeping was proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 按《國史》，開元五年正月二日，太廟四室摧毀，時神主皆存，迎奉於太極殿安置，玄宗素服避正殿。

translations.literal: According to the 《National History》, on the second day of the first month of the fifth year of Kaiyuan, four chambers of the Grand Temple collapsed. At the time, all the spirit tablets survived; they were respectfully received and placed in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and Xuanzong wore plain clothing and avoided the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: The 《National History》 records: Kaiyuan 5, first month, second day, four Grand Temple chambers collapsed; the tablets were saved to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and Xuanzong mourned in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，肅宗還京師，以宗廟為賊所焚，於光順門外設次，向廟哭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, when Suzong returned to the capital, because the ancestral temple had been burned by rebels, he set up a station outside Guangshun Gate and wept toward the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying 1: when Suzong returned, rebels had burned the temple, so he wept toward it from a station outside Guangshun Gate.

sentences.zh: 歷檢故事，不見百官奉慰之儀。

translations.literal: Searching precedents through, one does not see the rite of the hundred officials coming to offer condolence.
translations.idiomatic: Precedents show no rite of officials offering formal condolence.

sentences.zh: 然上既素服避殿，百官奉慰，亦合情禮。

translations.literal: Yet since the emperor already wore plain dress and avoided the hall, the hundred officials offering condolence also fits sentiment and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with the emperor in mourning dress, officials' condolence was still fitting.

sentences.zh: 竊循故事，比附參詳，恐須宗正寺具宗廟焚毀及神主失墜事由奏，皇帝素服避殿，受慰訖，輟朝三日，下詔委少府監擇日依禮新造列聖神主。

translations.literal: We privately follow precedents and compare and examine in detail; we fear the Court of the Imperial Clan must report fully the burning of the ancestral temple and the loss of spirit tablets; the emperor in plain dress avoids the hall, receives condolence, then suspends court for three days, and issues an edict commissioning the Director of the Palace Workshops to choose a day by ritual to newly make the spirit tablets of the successive sages.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed: the clan court should report the disaster; the emperor mourn, receive officials' condolences, halt court three days, and order new sage tablets made on an auspicious day.

sentences.zh: 如此方似合宜。

translations.literal: Only thus does it seem fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Only thus would the rites be proper.

sentences.zh: 伏緣采栗須十一月，漸恐遲晚。」

translations.literal: We note that gathering chestnut wood requires the eleventh month; we gradually fear it will be late."
translations.idiomatic: Chestnut wood for tablets required the eleventh month, and they feared delay."

sentences.zh: 修奉使宰相鄭延昌具議，中書門下奏曰：「伏以前年冬再有震驚，俄然巡寺，主司宗祝，迫以蒼黃。

translations.literal: The restoration commissioner, Chancellor Zheng Yanchang, fully deliberated; the Secretariat memorialized, saying: "We note that last winter there were again shocks; suddenly the court moved to monasteries; the masters of sacrifice were pressed in haste.
translations.idiomatic: The restoration commissioner, Chancellor Zheng Yanchang, fully deliberated; the Secretariat memorialized, saying: "We note that last winter there were again shocks; suddenly the court moved to monasteries; the masters of sacrifice were pressed in haste.

sentences.zh: 伏緣移蹕鳳翔，未敢陳奏。

translations.literal: We note that because the court moved to Fengxiang, we did not dare memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: They had not yet reported while lodged at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 今則將回鑾輅，皆舉典章，清廟再營，孝思咸備。

translations.literal: Now the imperial carriage is about to return; all should uphold the canon; the pure temple will be rebuilt and filial thought fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Now the throne was returning, canon would be restored, and filial rebuilding of the temple could proceed.

sentences.zh: 伏請降敕，命所司參詳典禮修奉。」

translations.literal: We respectfully request an edict ordering the offices to examine the canon in detail and restore and maintain it."
translations.idiomatic: They asked for an edict ordering offices to restore the temple by canonical rites."

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「朕以涼德，祗嗣寶圖，不能上承天休，下正人紀，兵革競興於宇縣，車輿再越於籓垣，宗廟震驚，烝嘗廢闕。

translations.literal: The edict said: "With meager virtue, I reverently inherited the precious throne, but I have been unable above to receive Heaven's blessing and below to correct human order. Weapons and war have risen throughout the realm, the imperial carriage has twice gone beyond the borders, the ancestral temple was shaken, and the zheng and chang sacrifices were left undone.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "With meager virtue I inherited the throne, yet failed above to receive Heaven's favor and below to set human order right. War rose across the realm, the imperial carriage twice crossed the frontiers, the ancestral temple was shaken, and the seasonal sacrifices lapsed.

sentences.zh: 敬修典禮，倍切哀摧。

translations.literal: As we reverently repair the canonical rites, grief and devastation are doubly intense.
translations.idiomatic: As we reverently restore the rites, the grief is doubly sharp.

sentences.zh: 宜付所司。」

translations.literal: It should be referred to the responsible offices."
translations.idiomatic: Refer this to the responsible offices."

sentences.zh: 又修奉太廟使宰相鄭延昌奏：「太廟大殿十一室、二十三間、十一架，功績至大，計料支費不少。

translations.literal: Also, Zheng Yanchang, chancellor and commissioner for repairing and reverently restoring the Grand Temple, memorialized: "The main hall of the Grand Temple has eleven chambers, twenty-three bays, and eleven frames. The work is extremely great, and estimated expenditures are not small.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yanchang, the chancellor supervising restoration of the Grand Temple, also memorialized: "The main hall has eleven chambers, twenty-three bays, and eleven roof frames; the work is enormous, and the costs will be substantial.

sentences.zh: 兼宗廟制度有數，難為損益。

translations.literal: Moreover ancestral temple institutions have fixed numbers; it is hard to increase or decrease them.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral temple dimensions were fixed and hard to alter.

sentences.zh: 今不審依元料修奉，為復更有商量？

translations.literal: Now we do not know whether to restore according to the original estimates or again have further deliberation?
translations.idiomatic: Should restoration follow original plans or be renegotiated?

sentences.zh: 請下禮官詳議。」

translations.literal: We request sending it down to ritual officers for detailed deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: They requested that ritual officers be ordered to deliberate in detail."

sentences.zh: 太常博士殷盈孫奏議言：「如依元料，難以速成，況幣藏方虛，須資變禮。

translations.literal: Erudite Yin Yingsun memorialized, saying: "If we follow the original estimates, it will be hard to complete quickly; moreover the treasury of silks is empty—we must rely on altered ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Yin Yingsun memorialized, saying: "If we follow the original estimates, it will be hard to complete quickly; moreover the treasury of silks is empty—we must rely on altered ritual.

sentences.zh: 竊以，以新修太廟未成，其新造神主，權于長安殿安置，便行饗告之禮，如同宗廟之儀，以俟廟成，方為遷祔。

translations.literal: We privately hold that, because the newly repaired Grand Temple is not finished, the newly made spirit tablets should temporarily be placed in the Hall of Everlasting Peace, and the offering and announcement rites carried out as in the ancestral temple, to await the temple's completion before enshrining.
translations.idiomatic: Until the new temple was done, new tablets should lodge in the Hall of Everlasting Peace for offering rites, then move when the temple stood.

sentences.zh: 今京城除充大內及正衙外，別無殿宇。

translations.literal: Now in the capital apart from filling the inner palace and main audience halls, there are no other halls.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from palace and audience halls, the capital had no spare halls.

sentences.zh: 伏聞先有詔旨，欲以少府監大廳權充太廟。

translations.literal: We have heard there was already an edict intending to use the great hall of the Director of the Palace Workshops as a temporary Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had proposed the Palace Workshops' great hall as a temporary temple.

sentences.zh: 其廳五間，伏緣十一室於五間之中陳設隘狹，請更接續修建，成十一間，以備十一室薦饗之所。

translations.literal: That hall has five bays; we note that setting out eleven chambers within five bays is cramped and narrow; we request further connected construction to make eleven bays as places for the eleven chambers' offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Five bays could not hold eleven shrines; they asked to extend the hall to eleven bays.

sentences.zh: 其三太后廟，即於少府監取西南屋三間，以備三室告饗所。」

translations.literal: The three empress-dowager temples should take three rooms in the southwest of the Director of the Palace Workshops as places for the three chambers' announcement offerings."
translations.idiomatic: The three empress-dowager temples should take three rooms in the southwest of the Director of the Palace Workshops as places for the three chambers' announcement offerings."

sentences.zh: 敕旨從之，

translations.literal: The edict followed,
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 大順元年，將行禘祭，有司請以三太后神主祔饗於太廟。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dashun, when the di sacrifice was about to be performed, the responsible offices requested that the spirit tablets of the three empress dowagers be enshrined for joint offering in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Dashun 1: before the di rite, officers proposed bringing the three empress-dowager tablets into the Grand Temple for joint offering.

sentences.zh: 三太后者，孝明太皇太后鄭氏，宣宗之母也；

translations.literal: The three empress dowagers were Grand Empress Dowager Xiaoming of the Zheng clan, Xuanzong's mother;
translations.idiomatic: The three were Grand Empress Dowager Xiaoming of the Zheng clan, Xuanzong's mother;

sentences.zh: 恭僖皇太后王氏，敬宗之母也；

translations.literal: Grand Empress Dowager Gongxi of the Wang clan, Jingzong's mother;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Empress Dowager Gongxi of the Wang clan, Jingzong's mother;

sentences.zh: 貞獻皇太后蕭氏，文宗之母也。

translations.literal: and Grand Empress Dowager Zhenxian of the Xiao clan, Wenzong's mother.
translations.idiomatic: and Grand Empress Dowager Zhenxian of the Xiao clan, Wenzong's mother.

sentences.zh: 三后之崩，皆作神主，有故不當入太廟。

translations.literal: When the three empresses died, spirit tablets were all made; for reasons they should not enter the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Each had a tablet at death but should not enter the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 當時禮官建議並置別廟，每年五享，及三年一祫，五年一禘，皆於本廟行事，無奉神主入太廟之文。

translations.literal: At the time ritual officers proposed establishing separate temples for all, with five offerings yearly and cha every three years and di every five years—all conducted at their own temples, with no text of bringing spirit tablets into the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers had placed them in separate temples with their own seasonal and cha/di rites, never bringing tablets into the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 至是亂離之後，舊章散失，禮院憑《曲臺禮》，欲以三太后祔享太廟。

translations.literal: At this time after the turmoil, the old regulations were scattered and lost; the Ritual Institute relied on Wang Yanwei's 《Quetai Rites》 and wished to enshrine the three empress dowagers in joint offering at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion, the Ritual Institute, citing the 《Quetai Rites》, sought to joint-offer the three empress dowagers in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 博士殷盈孫獻議非之，曰：臣謹按三太后，憲宗、穆宗之后也。二帝已祔太廟，三后所以立別廟者，不可入太廟故也。與帝在位，皇后別廟不同。今有司悮用王彥威《曲臺禮》，禘別廟太后于太廟，乖戾之甚。臣竊究事體，有五不可。:《曲臺禮》云：「別廟皇后，禘祫於太廟，祔于祖姑之下。」此乃皇后先崩，已造神主，夫在帝位，如昭成、肅明、元獻、昭德之比。昭成、肅明之崩也，睿宗在位。元獻之崩也，玄宗在位。昭德之崩也，肅宗在位。四后於太廟未有本室，故創別廟，當為太廟合食之主，故禘祫乃奉以入饗。其神主但題云「某諡皇后」，明其後太廟有本室，即當遷祔，帝方在位，故皇后暫立別廟耳。本是太廟合食之祖，故禘祫乃升，太廟未有位，故祔祖姑之下。今恭僖、貞獻二太后，皆穆宗之后。恭僖，會昌四年造神主，合祔穆宗廟室。時穆宗廟已祔武宗母宣懿皇后神主，故為恭僖別立廟，其神主直題云皇太后，明其終安別廟，不入太廟故也。貞獻太后，大中元年作神主，立別廟，其神主亦題為太后，並與恭僖義同。孝明，咸通五年作神主，合祔憲宗廟室。憲宗廟已祔穆宗之母懿安皇后，故孝明亦別立廟，是懿宗祖母，故題其主為太皇太后。與恭僖、貞獻亦同，帝在位，后先作神主之例。今以別廟太后神主，禘祭升享太廟，一不可也。:《曲臺禮別廟皇后禘祫于太廟儀注》云：「內常侍奉別廟皇后神主，入置於廟庭，赤黃褥位。奏云『某諡皇后禘祫祔享太廟』，然後以神主升。」今即須奏云「某諡太皇太后」。且太廟中皇后神主二十一室，今忽乙太皇太后入列于昭穆，二不可也。:若但云「某諡皇后」，則與所題都異，神何依憑？此三不可也。:《古今禮要》云：「舊典，周立姜嫄別廟，四時祭薦，及禘祫於七廟，皆祭。惟不入太祖廟為別配。魏文思甄后，明帝母，廟及寢依姜嫄之廟，四時及禘皆與諸廟同。」此舊禮明文，得以為證。今以別廟太后禘祫于太廟，四不可也。:所以置別廟太后，以孝明不可與懿安並祔憲宗之室，今禘享乃處懿安于舅姑之上，此五不可也。且祫，合祭也。合猶不入太祖之廟，而況於禘乎？竊以為並皆禘於別廟為宜。且恭僖、貞獻二廟，比在朱陽坊，禘、祫赴太廟，皆須備法駕，典禮甚重，儀衛至多。咸通之時，累遇大饗，耳目相接，歲代未遙，人皆見聞，事可詢訪，非敢以臆斷也。或曰：「以三廟故禘、袷於別廟，或可矣，而將來有可疑焉。謹案睿宗親盡已祧，今昭成、肅明二后同在夾室，如或後代憲宗、穆宗親盡而祧，三太后神主其得不入夾室乎？若遇禘、袷，則如之何？」對曰：此又大誤也。三太后廟若親盡合祧，但當閟而不享，安得處於夾室。禘、祫則就別廟行之，歷代已來，何嘗有別廟神主復入太廟夾室乎？禘、袷，禮之大者，無宜錯失。

translations.literal: Erudite Yin Yingsun presented a memorial opposing it, saying: Your servant has carefully examined the three empress dowagers: they are the consorts of Xianzong and Muzong. The two emperors have already been attached in the Great Temple. The reason separate temples were established for the three empress dowagers was that they could not enter the Great Temple. This differs from a separate temple for an empress while the emperor is on the throne. Now the responsible offices have mistakenly used Wang Yanwei's Qutai Rites and would perform the di sacrifice for empress dowagers of separate temples in the Great Temple; this is extremely perverse. Your servant has privately investigated the substance of the matter, and there are five reasons it cannot be done. First, the Qutai Rites says: "For an empress of a separate temple, at the di and xia sacrifices in the Great Temple, she is attached and feasted below the ancestral mother." This refers to an empress who died first and whose spirit tablet had already been made while her husband was on the imperial throne, such as Zhaocheng, Suming, Yuanxian, and Zhaode. When Zhaocheng and Suming died, Ruizong was on the throne. When Yuanxian died, Xuanzong was on the throne. When Zhaode died, Suzong was on the throne. These four empresses did not yet have their proper chambers in the Great Temple, so separate temples were created for them. They were to be tablets that would share food in the Great Temple, and therefore at di and xia they were brought in for the feast. Their spirit tablets were simply inscribed "Empress with such-and-such posthumous title," making clear that once they later had proper chambers in the Great Temple, they should be moved and attached there. Because the emperor was still on the throne, an empress only temporarily had a separate temple. She was originally an ancestor meant to share food in the Great Temple, and so she was raised at di and xia; since the Great Temple did not yet have a place for her, she was attached below the ancestral mother. Now Empress Dowagers Gongxi and Zhenxian are both consorts of Muzong. For Gongxi, a spirit tablet was made in the fourth year of Huichang, and she should have been attached in Muzong's temple chamber. At that time, Muzong's temple had already attached the spirit tablet of Wuzong's mother, Empress Xuanyi, and therefore a separate temple was established for Gongxi. Her spirit tablet was directly inscribed Empress Dowager, making clear that she would finally rest in a separate temple and would not enter the Great Temple. For Empress Dowager Zhenxian, a spirit tablet was made in the first year of Dazhong and a separate temple was established; her spirit tablet was also inscribed as Empress Dowager, and her meaning is the same as Gongxi's. For Xiaoming, a spirit tablet was made in the fifth year of Xiantong, and she should have been attached in Xianzong's temple chamber. Xianzong's temple had already attached the spirit tablet of Muzong's mother, Empress Yi'an, and therefore Xiaoming also had a separate temple. Since she was Yizong's grandmother, her tablet was inscribed as Grand Empress Dowager. This is also the same as Gongxi and Zhenxian, and not the precedent of an empress whose spirit tablet is made first while the emperor is on the throne. Now to take the spirit tablets of empress dowagers of separate temples and raise them to share in the di sacrifice in the Great Temple is the first reason it cannot be done. Second, the Ritual Notes for Di and Xia in the Great Temple for Empresses of Separate Temples in the Qutai Rites says: "The Palace Regular Attendant reverently carries the spirit tablet of the empress of the separate temple and sets it in the temple court on a red-yellow mat. He announces, 'The empress with such-and-such posthumous title is attached to share in the di and xia feast in the Great Temple,' and only afterward raises the spirit tablet." Now one would have to announce "the Grand Empress Dowager with such-and-such posthumous title." Moreover, within the Great Temple there are twenty-one chambers of empresses' spirit tablets; suddenly placing a Grand Empress Dowager in the zhao-mu sequence is the second reason it cannot be done. Third, if one merely says "Empress with such-and-such posthumous title," then it differs entirely from what is inscribed on the tablet; on what could the spirit rely? This is the third reason it cannot be done. Fourth, the Essentials of Ancient and Modern Ritual says: "The old canon says that Zhou established a separate temple for Jiang Yuan, with seasonal sacrifices and offerings, and that at di and xia in the seven temples she was sacrificed to in all of them, only not entering the temple of the Grand Ancestor as a separate consort. Empress Wensi Zhen of Wei, mother of Emperor Ming, had her temple and sleeping hall according to Jiang Yuan's temple; seasonal rites and di were all the same as in the other temples." This old ritual has clear text and may be used as evidence. Now to perform di and xia for empress dowagers of separate temples in the Great Temple is the fourth reason it cannot be done. Fifth, the reason separate temples were established for the empress dowagers was that Xiaoming could not be attached together with Yi'an in Xianzong's chamber. Now in the di feast, Yi'an would be placed above her husband's parents. This is the fifth reason it cannot be done. Moreover xia is a combined sacrifice. If even in combining they do not enter the temple of the Grand Ancestor, how much less should they do so at di? I privately consider that all of them should perform di in their separate temples. Also, the two temples of Gongxi and Zhenxian were nearby in Zhuyang Ward; when di and xia went to the Great Temple, full imperial processions had to be prepared, the ritual was very weighty, and the ceremonial guards were extremely numerous. In Xiantong, great feasts were repeatedly encountered; eyes and ears were connected to them, the years and generations are not remote, and people all saw and heard it. The matter can be investigated by inquiry; I do not dare decide it from private conjecture. Someone may say: "Because there are three temples, performing di and xia in the separate temples may be acceptable, but there will be a doubtful matter in the future. Carefully considering that Ruizong's kinship is exhausted and he has already been removed, now Empresses Zhaocheng and Suming are both in the side chamber. If in later generations Xianzong's and Muzong's kinship is exhausted and they are removed, can the spirit tablets of the three empress dowagers fail to enter the side chamber? If di or xia occurs, what then?" I answer: this too is a great error. If the three empress-dowager temples reach the point where kinship is exhausted and they should be removed, they should simply be closed and not feasted; how could they be placed in the side chamber? Di and xia should be performed at the separate temples. Since the successive dynasties, when has there ever been a case of spirit tablets from separate temples again entering the side chambers of the Great Temple? Di and xia are great matters of ritual, and they must not be wrongly handled.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Yin Yingsun presented a memorial opposing it, saying: Your servant has carefully examined the three empress dowagers: they are the consorts of Xianzong and Muzong. The two emperors have already been attached in the Great Temple. The reason separate temples were established for the three empress dowagers was that they could not enter the Great Temple. This differs from a separate temple for an empress while the emperor is on the throne. Now the responsible offices have mistakenly used Wang Yanwei's Qutai Rites and would perform the di sacrifice for empress dowagers of separate temples in the Great Temple; this is extremely perverse. Your servant has privately investigated the substance of the matter, and there are five reasons it cannot be done. First, the Qutai Rites says: "For an empress of a separate temple, at the di and xia sacrifices in the Great Temple, she is attached and feasted below the ancestral mother." This refers to an empress who died first and whose spirit tablet had already been made while her husband was on the imperial throne, such as Zhaocheng, Suming, Yuanxian, and Zhaode. When Zhaocheng and Suming died, Ruizong was on the throne. When Yuanxian died, Xuanzong was on the throne. When Zhaode died, Suzong was on the throne. These four empresses did not yet have their proper chambers in the Great Temple, so separate temples were created for them. They were to be tablets that would share food in the Great Temple, and therefore at di and xia they were brought in for the feast. Their spirit tablets were simply inscribed "Empress with such-and-such posthumous title," making clear that once they later had proper chambers in the Great Temple, they should be moved and attached there. Because the emperor was still on the throne, an empress only temporarily had a separate temple. She was originally an ancestor meant to share food in the Great Temple, and so she was raised at di and xia; since the Great Temple did not yet have a place for her, she was attached below the ancestral mother. Now Empress Dowagers Gongxi and Zhenxian are both consorts of Muzong. For Gongxi, a spirit tablet was made in the fourth year of Huichang, and she should have been attached in Muzong's temple chamber. At that time, Muzong's temple had already attached the spirit tablet of Wuzong's mother, Empress Xuanyi, and therefore a separate temple was established for Gongxi. Her spirit tablet was directly inscribed Empress Dowager, making clear that she would finally rest in a separate temple and would not enter the Great Temple. For Empress Dowager Zhenxian, a spirit tablet was made in the first year of Dazhong and a separate temple was established; her spirit tablet was also inscribed as Empress Dowager, and her meaning is the same as Gongxi's. For Xiaoming, a spirit tablet was made in the fifth year of Xiantong, and she should have been attached in Xianzong's temple chamber. Xianzong's temple had already attached the spirit tablet of Muzong's mother, Empress Yi'an, and therefore Xiaoming also had a separate temple. Since she was Yizong's grandmother, her tablet was inscribed as Grand Empress Dowager. This is also the same as Gongxi and Zhenxian, and not the precedent of an empress whose spirit tablet is made first while the emperor is on the throne. Now to take the spirit tablets of empress dowagers of separate temples and raise them to share in the di sacrifice in the Great Temple is the first reason it cannot be done. Second, the Ritual Notes for Di and Xia in the Great Temple for Empresses of Separate Temples in the Qutai Rites says: "The Palace Regular Attendant reverently carries the spirit tablet of the empress of the separate temple and sets it in the temple court on a red-yellow mat. He announces, 'The empress with such-and-such posthumous title is attached to share in the di and xia feast in the Great Temple,' and only afterward raises the spirit tablet." Now one would have to announce "the Grand Empress Dowager with such-and-such posthumous title." Moreover, within the Great Temple there are twenty-one chambers of empresses' spirit tablets; suddenly placing a Grand Empress Dowager in the zhao-mu sequence is the second reason it cannot be done. Third, if one merely says "Empress with such-and-such posthumous title," then it differs entirely from what is inscribed on the tablet; on what could the spirit rely? This is the third reason it cannot be done. Fourth, the Essentials of Ancient and Modern Ritual says: "The old canon says that Zhou established a separate temple for Jiang Yuan, with seasonal sacrifices and offerings, and that at di and xia in the seven temples she was sacrificed to in all of them, only not entering the temple of the Grand Ancestor as a separate consort. Empress Wensi Zhen of Wei, mother of Emperor Ming, had her temple and sleeping hall according to Jiang Yuan's temple; seasonal rites and di were all the same as in the other temples." This old ritual has clear text and may be used as evidence. Now to perform di and xia for empress dowagers of separate temples in the Great Temple is the fourth reason it cannot be done. Fifth, the reason separate temples were established for the empress dowagers was that Xiaoming could not be attached together with Yi'an in Xianzong's chamber. Now in the di feast, Yi'an would be placed above her husband's parents. This is the fifth reason it cannot be done. Moreover xia is a combined sacrifice. If even in combining they do not enter the temple of the Grand Ancestor, how much less should they do so at di? I privately consider that all of them should perform di in their separate temples. Also, the two temples of Gongxi and Zhenxian were nearby in Zhuyang Ward; when di and xia went to the Great Temple, full imperial processions had to be prepared, the ritual was very weighty, and the ceremonial guards were extremely numerous. In Xiantong, great feasts were repeatedly encountered; eyes and ears were connected to them, the years and generations are not remote, and people all saw and heard it. The matter can be investigated by inquiry; I do not dare decide it from private conjecture. Someone may say: "Because there are three temples, performing di and xia in the separate temples may be acceptable, but there will be a doubtful matter in the future. Carefully considering that Ruizong's kinship is exhausted and he has already been removed, now Empresses Zhaocheng and Suming are both in the side chamber. If in later generations Xianzong's and Muzong's kinship is exhausted and they are removed, can the spirit tablets of the three empress dowagers fail to enter the side chamber? If di or xia occurs, what then?" I answer: this too is a great error. If the three empress-dowager temples reach the point where kinship is exhausted and they should be removed, they should simply be closed and not feasted; how could they be placed in the side chamber? Di and xia should be performed at the separate temples. Since the successive dynasties, when has there ever been a case of spirit tablets from separate temples again entering the side chambers of the Great Temple? Di and xia are great matters of ritual, and they must not be wrongly handled.

sentences.zh: 宰相孔緯曰：「博士之言是也。

translations.literal: Chancellor Kong Wei said: "The erudite's words are correct.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Kong Wei said: "The erudite's words are correct.

sentences.zh: 昨禮院所奏儀注，今已敕下，大祭日迫，不可遽改，且依行之。」

translations.literal: Yesterday the Ritual Institute's submitted protocol has now been issued an edict down; the great sacrifice day presses—it cannot be suddenly changed; for the time being let it be carried out as submitted."
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday the Ritual Institute's submitted protocol has now been issued an edict down; the great sacrifice day presses—it cannot be suddenly changed; for the time being let it be carried out as submitted."

sentences.zh: 於是遂以三太后祔祫太廟。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three empress dowagers were enshrined in cha at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The three empress dowagers were nonetheless enshrined in the Grand Temple cha rite.

sentences.zh: 達禮者譏其大謬，至今未正。

translations.literal: Those versed in ritual mocked the great error; it has not been corrected to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual experts condemned the blunder, still uncorrected.

sentences.zh: 十一月，太常博士任疇上言：「去月十七日，饗德明、興聖廟，得廟直候論狀，稱懿祖室在獻祖室之上，當時雖以為然，便依行事，猶牒報監察使及宗正寺，請過示詳窺玉牒，如有不同，即相知聞奏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Erudite Ren Chou submitted, saying: "On the seventeenth of last month, offering at the Deming and Xingsheng temples, we received a report from the temple attendant Hou Lun's petition, stating that the chamber of Emperor Yi was above the chamber of Emperor Xian; though it was then deemed correct and the rite was performed, we still dispatched notice to the surveillance commissioner and the Court of the Imperial Clan, requesting examination of the imperial genealogy; if there is any difference, inform each other and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Erudite Ren Chou submitted, saying: "On the seventeenth of last month, offering at the Deming and Xingsheng temples, we received a report from the temple attendant Hou Lun's petition, stating that the chamber of Emperor Yi was above the chamber of Emperor Xian; though it was then deemed correct and the rite was performed, we still dispatched notice to the surveillance commissioner and the Court of the Imperial Clan, requesting examination of the imperial genealogy; if there is any difference, inform each other and memorialize.

sentences.zh: 爾後伏檢《高祖神堯皇帝本紀》，伏審獻祖為懿祖之昭，懿祖為獻祖之穆，昭穆之位，天地極殊。

translations.literal: Thereafter your subject examined the 《Basic Annals of the Divine Yao Emperor Gaozu》 and found that the Ancestor of Offerings was the zhao of the Ancestor of Eminence, and the Ancestor of Eminence was the mu of the Ancestor of Offerings--the positions of zhao and mu are as far apart as Heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject found in the 《Basic Annals of the Divine Yao Emperor Gaozu》 that the Ancestor of Offerings was zhao to the Ancestor of Eminence and the Ancestor of Eminence was mu to the Ancestor of Offerings--zhao and mu stand as far apart as heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 今廟室奪倫，不即陳奏，然尚為苟且，罪不容誅。

translations.literal: Now the temple chambers usurp proper order, yet it was not reported at once; still to temporize is an offense that brooks no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The shrine order is violated yet was not reported; to temporize is unpardonable.

sentences.zh: 仍敕修撰朱儔、檢討王皞研精詳復，得報稱：『，制追尊咎繇為德明皇帝，涼武昭王為興聖皇帝。

translations.literal: An edict still ordered Compiler Zhu Chou and Reviewer Wang Hao to examine with care; the reply stated: "In the second year of Zhide, an edict posthumously honored Gao Yao as Emperor Deming and the Martial Illustrious King of Liang as Emperor Xingsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Chou and Wang Hao were ordered to review; the reply cited Zhide 2: Gao Yao was made Emperor Deming and the Liang Martial Illustrious King Emperor Xingsheng.

sentences.zh: 十載，立廟。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, temples were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year temples were set up.

sentences.zh: 至貞元十九年，制從給事中陳京、右僕射姚南仲等一百五十人之議，以為禘、袷是祖宗以序之祭，凡有國者必尊太祖。

translations.literal: By the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan, an edict followed the deliberation of 150 men led by Supervising Secretary Chen Jing and Right Vice Director Yao Nanzhong, holding that the di and jia sacrifices are ordered sacrifices to the ancestors and that every state must honor its Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhenyuan 19, the court followed Chen Jing, Yao Nanzhong, and 150 others: di and jia are ordered ancestral rites, and every state honors its Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 今國家以景皇帝為太祖，太祖之上，施於禘、袷，不可為位。

translations.literal: Now the state takes Emperor Jing as Grand Ancestor; above the Grand Ancestor, no position may be established for the di and jia rites.
translations.idiomatic: The state takes Emperor Jing as Grand Ancestor; above him no place may be made in the di and jia rites.

sentences.zh: 請按德明、興聖廟共成四室，祔遷獻、懿二祖。』

translations.literal: We ask that according to the Deming and Xingsheng temples together forming four chambers, the Ancestors of Offerings and Eminence be enshrined and moved.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Deming and Xingsheng shrines form four chambers and receive the relocated Offerings and Eminence ancestors.

sentences.zh: 謹尋儔等所報，即當時表奏，並獻居懿上。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully traced what Chou and others reported—that was the memorial of the time—and all placed Offerings above Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Chou’s report was the original memorial: Offerings was always above Eminence.

sentences.zh: 伏以國之大事，宗廟為先，禘、祫之禮，不當失序。

translations.literal: Your subject notes that the great affairs of the state put the ancestral temple first; the rites of di and xia must not lose order.
translations.idiomatic: State affairs begin with the ancestral temple; di and xia must keep their order.

sentences.zh: 四十餘載，理難尋詰。

translations.literal: More than forty years have passed; it is hard to pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Forty years have passed—too late to trace easily.

sentences.zh: 伏祈聖鑒，即垂詔敕，具禮遷正。」

translations.literal: Your subject prays the sacred discernment may at once issue an edict and complete the rites of relocation and correction."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject prays the sacred discernment may at once issue an edict and complete the rites of relocation and correction."

sentences.zh: 其月，疇又奏曰：「伏聞今月十三日敕，以臣所奏獻、懿祖二室倒置事，宜令禮官集議聞奏者。

translations.literal: That month, Zhou again memorialized: "Your subject has heard that on the thirteenth of this month an edict, on your subject’s report of the inverted placement of the two chambers of the Ancestors of Offerings and Eminence, ordered the ritual officers to assemble for deliberation and report.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Zhou again memorialized: "Your subject has heard that on the thirteenth of this month an edict, on your subject’s report of the inverted placement of the two chambers of the Ancestors of Offerings and Eminence, ordered the ritual officers to assemble for deliberation and report.

sentences.zh: 臣去月十七日，緣遇太廟祫饗太祖景皇帝已下群主，准貞元十九年所祔獻、懿祖於德明廟，共為四室。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day of last month, when the xia offering in the Grand Temple was made to the spirit tablets from Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing downward, it followed the Zhenyuan 19 enshrinement of Xianzu and Yizu in the Deming Temple, making four chambers in all.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth last month, the Grand Temple xia for tablets from Emperor Jing down followed the Zhenyuan 19 placement of Xianzu and Yizu in Deming Temple, making four chambers.

sentences.zh: 准元敕，各於本室行享禮。

translations.literal: According to the original edict, each was to receive offerings in its own chamber.
translations.idiomatic: By the original edict each tablet was served in its own chamber.

sentences.zh: 審知獻祖合居懿祖之上，昭穆方正。

translations.literal: It was clear that the Ancestor of Offerings should stand above the Ancestor of Eminence and that zhao and mu were correct.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings should stand above Eminence—zhao and mu in proper order.

sentences.zh: 其時親見獻祖之室，倒居懿祖之下。

translations.literal: At the time your subject personally saw the chamber of the Ancestor of Offerings placed inverted below that of the Ancestor of Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: He saw Offerings’ chamber placed below Eminence’s.

sentences.zh: 於後遍校圖籍，實見差殊，遂敢聞奏。

translations.literal: Afterward, comparing registers throughout, the discrepancy was real; your subject therefore dared to report.
translations.idiomatic: Registers later confirmed the error; he reported it.

sentences.zh: 今奉敕宜令禮官集議聞奏者。

translations.literal: Now, receiving the edict that ritual officers should assemble for deliberation and report.
translations.idiomatic: Now the edict required ritual officers to debate and report.

sentences.zh: 臣得奉禮郎李岡、太祝柳仲年、協律郎諸葛畋李潼、檢討官王皞、修撰朱儔、博士閔慶之等七人伏稱：『謹按《高祖神堯皇帝本紀》及皇室圖譜，並武德、貞觀、永徽、開元已來諸禮著在甲令者，並云獻祖宣皇帝是神堯之高祖，懿祖光皇帝是神堯皇帝之曾祖，以高曾辨之，則獻祖是懿祖之父，懿祖是獻祖之子。

translations.literal: Your subject obtained seven men--Director of Offerings Li Gang, Grand Invocator Liu Zhongnian, Harmonizing Officer Zhuge Tian, Li Tong, Reviewer Wang Hao, Compiler Zhu Chou, and Erudite Min Qingzhi--who stated: 'Respectfully according to the 《Basic Annals of the Divine Yao Emperor Gaozu》 and the imperial genealogy, and all ritual codes recorded in statutes from Wude, Zhenguan, Yonghui, and Kaiyuan onward, all say that the Ancestor of Offerings Emperor Xuan was Gaozu's great-grandfather and the Ancestor of Eminence Emperor Guang was Gaozu's great-great-grandfather; by great-grandfather and great-great-grandfather, the Ancestor of Offerings was father to the Ancestor of Eminence and the Ancestor of Eminence was son to the Ancestor of Offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Seven officers--Li Gang, Liu Zhongnian, Zhuge Tian, Li Tong, Wang Hao, Zhu Chou, Min Qingzhi--cited the 《Basic Annals of the Divine Yao Emperor Gaozu》 and the genealogy: Offerings Xuan was Gaozu's great-grandfather, Eminence Guang his great-great-grandfather; Offerings was Eminence's father.

sentences.zh: 即博士任疇所奏倒祀不虛。

translations.literal: Thus Erudite Ren Zhou’s report of inverted sacrifice is not false.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhou’s charge of inverted worship was true.

sentences.zh: 臣等伏乞即垂詔敕，具禮遷正。』」。

translations.literal: Your subject prays that an edict be issued at once to complete the rites of relocation and correction.
translations.idiomatic: Your subjects humbly beg that an edict be issued at once to complete the rites of relocation and correction.'"

sentences.zh: 其事遂行。

translations.literal: The matter was then carried out.
translations.idiomatic: It was done.

sentences.zh: 僖宗自興元還京，夏四月，將行禘祭，有司引舊儀：「禘德明、興聖二廟，及懿祖、獻祖神主祔興聖、德明廟，通為四室。」

translations.literal: When Xizong returned to the capital from Xingyuan, in summer, fourth month, as the di sacrifice was about to be performed, the responsible offices cited the old rite: "Perform the di sacrifice at the two temples Deming and Xingsheng, and enshrine the spirit tablets of Yizu and Xianzu in Xingsheng and Deming temples, making four chambers in all."
translations.idiomatic: Xizong returned from Xingyuan; in summer's fourth month, before the di rite, offices cited old practice: "di at Deming and Xingsheng, with Offerings and Eminence in four chambers."

translations.literal: In the chaos of Huang Chao, the temples had been burned; when the di was now to be held, they were ordered to deliberate the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao had burned the temples; rites for the coming di had to be reworked.
