translations.literal: Erudite Yin Yingsun argued: "Your subject holds that the four temples of Deming and the rest achieved no founding merit and were posthumous ennoblements only; moreover they are extremely remote in date from the present emperor and very distant in zhao-mu.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Yin Yingsun argued: "Your subject holds that the four temples of Deming and the rest achieved no founding merit and were posthumous ennoblements only; moreover they are extremely remote in date from the present emperor and very distant in zhao-mu.

sentences.zh: 可依晉韋泓『屋毀乃已』之例，因而廢之。」

translations.literal: One may follow the Jin precedent of Wei Hong, "when the house is destroyed, stop," and abolish them."
translations.idiomatic: Follow Wei Hong’s Jin rule: when the building is gone, cease—and abolish them.

sentences.zh: 敕下百僚都省會議，禮部員外薛昭緯奏議曰：伏以禮貴從宜，過猶不及，祀有常典，理當據經。

translations.literal: The edict was sent down for all officials to meet in the Department of State Affairs, and Xue Zhaowei, Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, memorialized: I submit that ritual values adapting to what is fitting; excess is like insufficiency. Sacrifice has constant canons, and principle should rest on the classics.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was referred to the officials in the Department of State Affairs. Xue Zhaowei of the Ministry of Rites memorialized that ritual must fit the occasion, neither exceeding nor falling short, and that sacrifice should follow the classics.

sentences.zh: 謹按德明追尊，實為遐遠，徵諸歷代，莫有其倫。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering Deming's posthumous honoring, it is truly remote; when examined through the successive ages, nothing is comparable to it.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the posthumous honoring of Deming was extraordinarily remote, with no parallel in earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 自古典禮該詳，無逾周室。

translations.literal: From antiquity, no ritual code has been more complete and detailed than that of the Zhou house.
translations.idiomatic: Among ancient ritual systems, none was more complete than that of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 后稷實始封之祖，文王乃建極之君，且不聞后稷之前，別議立廟。

translations.literal: Hou Ji was truly the ancestor first enfeoffed, and King Wen was the lord who established the royal pivot; moreover, one does not hear that before Hou Ji they separately discussed establishing temples.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Ji was the first enfeoffed ancestor and King Wen the founder of royal order; no separate temples were proposed for ancestors before Hou Ji.

sentences.zh: 以至二漢則可明徵劉累，梁、魏則近有蕭、曹，稽彼簡書，並無追號。

translations.literal: Coming down to the two Han, Liu Lei can be clearly cited; for Liang and Wei, there are nearer examples in Xiao and Cao. Examining those records, none had a posthumous title added.
translations.idiomatic: The Han could trace themselves to Liu Lei, and Liang and Wei to the Xiao and Cao lines, yet their records show no such retroactive honorifics.

sentences.zh: 迨於興聖，事非有據。

translations.literal: As for Xingsheng, the matter has no evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The case for Xingsheng had no evidentiary basis.

sentences.zh: 蓋以始王於涼，遂列為祖。

translations.literal: It was only because he first became king in Liang that he was then listed as an ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: He was listed as an ancestor merely because he had first ruled in Liang.

sentences.zh: 類長沙於後漢之代，等楚元于宋高之朝，悉無尊禮之名，足為憲章之驗。

translations.literal: He is like Changsha in the Later Han line and equivalent to Yuan of Chu in the court of Gao of Song; all lacked names of honored ritual, which is sufficient as evidence for regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Comparable figures, such as Changsha for Later Han and Yuan of Chu for Emperor Gao of Song, received no such ritual honors; these cases supply the precedent.

sentences.zh: 重以獻祖、懿祖，皆非宗有德而祖有功，親盡宜祧，理當毀瘞，行於二廟，亦出一時。

translations.literal: Moreover, Xianzu and Yizu were neither zong with virtue nor zu with merit. When kinship was exhausted they should be moved out; by principle they should be destroyed and buried. Their placement in the two temples also arose at one time.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu and Yizu were neither meritorious ancestors nor virtuous temple founders; once their kinship line was exhausted, ritual required removal and burial, and their two temples were only a temporary measure.

sentences.zh: 且武德之初，議宗廟之事，神堯聽之，太宗參之，碩學通儒，森然在列，而不議立皋陶、涼武昭之廟，蓋知其非所宜立也。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the beginning of Wude, when ancestral-temple matters were discussed, Shenyao heard them and Taizong participated; eminent scholars and learned classicists stood densely in attendance, yet they did not discuss establishing temples for Gao Yao or Liang Wuzhao, because they knew these should not be established.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wude, Gaozu and Taizong considered the temple system with many eminent classicists present, yet no one proposed temples for Gao Yao or Liang Wuzhao, because they knew such temples were improper.

sentences.zh: 尊太祖、代祖為帝，而以獻祖為宣簡公，懿祖為懿王，卒不加帝號者，謂其親盡則毀明矣。

translations.literal: They honored Taizu and Daizu as emperors, but made Xianzu Duke Xuanjian and Yizu King Yi, and in the end did not add imperial titles; this shows clearly that when kinship was exhausted they were to be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu and Daizu were honored as emperors, while Xianzu remained Duke Xuanjian and Yizu King Yi; the lack of imperial titles shows they were meant to be removed when kinship ended.

sentences.zh: 《春秋左氏傳》：「孔子在陳，聞魯廟災。

translations.literal: 《Chunqiu Zuoshi zhuan》 says: "When Confucius was in Chen, he heard of a fire in the Lu temple.
translations.idiomatic: 《Chunqiu Zuoshi zhuan》 says: "When Confucius was in Chen, he heard that the Lu temple had burned.

sentences.zh: 曰：『其桓僖乎？』

translations.literal: He said, 'Was it Huan and Xi?'
translations.idiomatic: He asked, 'Was it Huan and Xi?'

sentences.zh: 已而果然。」

translations.literal: Afterward it was indeed so."
translations.idiomatic: It later proved to be so."

sentences.zh: 蓋以親盡不毀，宜致天災，炯然之徵，不可忽也。

translations.literal: This was because when kinship was exhausted and the temples were not destroyed, it was fitting that heavenly disaster arrived; this bright evidence cannot be ignored.
translations.idiomatic: The point is that failing to remove temples after kinship ends can bring heavenly disaster; the evidence is clear and cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 據太常禮院狀所引至德二年克復後不作弘農府君廟神主，及晉韋泓「屋朽乃已」之議，頗為明據，深協禮經。

translations.literal: According to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Institute statement, which cited that after the recovery in Zhide 2 no spirit tablet was made for Duke Hongnong, and also cited Wei Hong of Jin's proposal, "when the building decays, then stop," there is rather clear evidence, deeply agreeing with the ritual classics.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Institute cited clear evidence: after the restoration in Zhide 2 no tablet was made for Duke Hongnong, and Wei Hong of Jin had argued, "when the building decays, then stop." These points accord with the ritual classics.

sentences.zh: 其興聖等四室，請依禮院之議。

translations.literal: As for the four chambers including Xingsheng, I request that the proposal of the Ritual Institute be followed.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that the four chambers, including Xingsheng, follow the Ritual Institute's proposal.

sentences.zh: 奉敕敬依典禮，付所司。

translations.literal: Receiving the edict, we respectfully follow the canonical rites and refer the matter to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed the canon and referred execution to the offices.

sentences.zh: 開元二十二年正月，制以籩、豆之薦，或未能備物，宜令禮官學士詳議具奏。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-second year of Kaiyuan, an edict held that in the offering of baskets and bean-vessels, some items might not be complete; ritual officers and academicians were to deliberate in detail and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 22, first month: an edict said basket-and-bean offerings might be incomplete and ordered ritual scholars to report.

sentences.zh: 太常卿韋縚請「宗廟之奠，每室籩、豆各加十二。

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Zou requested: "For offerings in the ancestral temple, let each chamber have twelve baskets and twelve beans added.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Zou requested: "For offerings in the ancestral temple, let each chamber have twelve baskets and twelve beans added.

sentences.zh: 又今之酌獻酒爵，制度全小，僅無一合，執持甚難，請稍令廣大。

translations.literal: Moreover the present wine cups for libation are wholly small, barely one he in measure, and very hard to hold; we ask that they be made somewhat larger.
translations.idiomatic: Libation cups were tiny—barely one he—and hard to hold; he asked they be enlarged.

sentences.zh: 其郊祀奠獻，亦准此。

translations.literal: Suburban and border offerings should follow this as well.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban offerings should follow the same rule.

sentences.zh: 仍望付尚書省集眾官詳議，務從折衷。」

translations.literal: We also hope the Department of State Affairs may gather all officials for detailed deliberation and seek a balanced mean."
translations.idiomatic: We also hope the Department of State Affairs may gather all officials for detailed deliberation and seek a balanced mean."

sentences.zh: 於是兵部侍郎張均及職方郎中韋述等建議曰：謹按《禮祭統》曰：「凡天之所生，地之所長，苟可薦者，莫不咸在。

translations.literal: Thereupon Vice Minister of War Zhang Jun, Director of the Bureau of Operations Wei Shu, and others proposed: Respectfully, according to 《Li Jitong》, "Of all that Heaven produces and Earth grows, if it can be offered, nothing is not present.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, Wei Shu, and the others answered by citing 《Li Jitong》: "All things produced by Heaven and grown by Earth may be included when they are fit to offer.

sentences.zh: 水草陸海，三牲八簋，昆蟲之異，草木之實，陰陽之物，皆備薦矣。」

translations.literal: Water plants and land and sea products, the three sacrificial animals and eight grain vessels, strange insects, fruits of plants and trees, and things of yin and yang are all fully offered."
translations.idiomatic: Water plants, goods of land and sea, sacrificial animals, grain vessels, unusual creatures, fruits, and all things of yin and yang are provided for the offering."

sentences.zh: 聖人知孝子之情深，而物類之無限，故為之節制，使祭有常禮，物有其品，器有其數。

translations.literal: The sages knew that the feelings of filial sons were deep and that the categories of things were without limit, so they made regulations for them, causing sacrifices to have constant rites, objects to have their grades, and vessels to have their numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The sages knew filial feeling was deep but the range of possible offerings was endless, so they regulated sacrifice with fixed rites, ranked offerings, and counted vessels.

sentences.zh: 上自天子，下至公卿，貴賤差降，無相逾越，百代常行無易之道也。

translations.literal: Above, from the Son of Heaven, down to dukes and ministers, noble and base differ by descending grades and do not overstep one another; this is the constant way practiced for a hundred generations and not changed.
translations.idiomatic: From the emperor down through the high ministers, rank determined what could be used, with no overstepping. This was the enduring rule of successive ages.

sentences.zh: 又按《周禮•膳夫》，「掌王之食飲膳羞：食用六穀，膳用六牲，飲用六清，羞用百有二十品，珍用八物，醬用百有二十甕」，則與祭祀之物，豐省本殊。

translations.literal: Again, according to 《Zhouli: Shanfu》, "He manages the king's foods, drinks, viands, and delicacies: food uses the six grains, viands use the six animals, drinks use the six clear liquors, delicacies use 120 kinds, rarities use eight things, and sauces use 120 jars"; thus these and the things of sacrifice differ fundamentally in abundance and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: 《Zhouli: Shanfu》 says: "The officer manages the king's foods, drinks, viands, and delicacies," with many grains, animals, drinks, delicacies, rarities, and sauces; this shows that royal meals and sacrificial offerings differed by nature in abundance and restraint.

sentences.zh: 《左傳》曰：「享以訓恭儉，宴以示慈惠，恭儉以行禮，慈惠以布政。」

translations.literal: 《Zuozhuan》 says: "The formal offering teaches reverence and frugality; the banquet displays kindness and favor. Reverence and frugality carry out ritual; kindness and favor spread government."
translations.idiomatic: 《Zuozhuan》 says: "Formal offerings teach reverence and restraint; banquets display kindness and grace; reverence and restraint carry out ritual, and kindness and grace spread government."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「享有體薦，宴有折俎。」

translations.literal: It also says: "At formal offerings there are whole-body presentations; at banquets there are cut-up stands."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Formal offerings present whole victims; banquets serve cut meat."

sentences.zh: 杜預曰：「享有體薦，爵盈而不飲，豆乾而不食，宴則相與食之。」

translations.literal: Du Yu said: "At formal offerings there are whole-body presentations; the cup is full but not drunk, and the dishes are dry but not eaten. At banquets, people eat them together."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu explains: "In formal offerings the cup is filled but not drunk, and the dishes are set out but not eaten; at banquets, the participants eat together."

sentences.zh: 享之與宴，猶且異文，祭奠所陳，固不同矣。

translations.literal: If offerings and banquets even have different wording, then what is set out in sacrifices and libations is certainly not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Since even the terminology separates offerings from banquets, sacrificial displays plainly should not be treated as ordinary meals.

sentences.zh: 又按《周禮》，籩人、豆人，各掌四籩、四豆之實，供祭祀與賓客，所用各殊。

translations.literal: Again, according to 《Zhouli》, the officers of baskets and dishes each manage the contents of the four baskets and four dishes, supplying sacrifices and guests, and the things used in each are different.
translations.idiomatic: 《Zhouli》 also assigns separate basket and dish offerings for sacrifices and for guests, with different contents for each use.

sentences.zh: 據此數文，祭奠不同常時，其來久矣。

translations.literal: On the basis of these several texts, sacrifices and libations have differed from ordinary occasions for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: These passages show that sacrificial offerings have long been distinct from everyday food.

sentences.zh: 且人之嗜好，本無憑准，宴私之饌，與時遷移。

translations.literal: Moreover, human tastes and preferences have no fixed standard, and the dishes of private feasts shift with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Personal tastes have no stable rule, and private banquet fare changes from age to age.

sentences.zh: 故聖人一切同歸于古，難平生所嗜，非禮亦不薦也；

translations.literal: Therefore the sages in all cases returned them to antiquity; even what one liked in life, if it was not ritual, was not offered;
translations.idiomatic: The sages therefore brought sacrifice back to ancient norms: even favorite foods from life were not offered if they did not accord with ritual;

sentences.zh: 平生所惡，是禮即不去也。

translations.literal: what one disliked in life, if it was ritual, was not removed.
translations.idiomatic: and even disliked foods were retained if ritual required them.

sentences.zh: 《楚語》曰：「屈到嗜芰，有疾，召宗老而屬曰：『祭我必以芰。』

translations.literal: 《Discourses of Chu》 says: "Qu Dao liked water chestnuts. When ill, he summoned the clan elders and instructed them, saying, 'When sacrificing to me, be sure to use water chestnuts.'
translations.idiomatic: 《Discourses of Chu》 records that Qu Dao loved water chestnuts and, when sick, told the clan elders, 'Use water chestnuts in my sacrifices.'

sentences.zh: 及卒，宗老將薦芰，屈建命去之，曰：『祭典有之，國君有牛享，大夫有羊饋，士有豚犬之奠，庶人有魚炙之薦，籩豆脯醢，則上下安之。

translations.literal: When he died, the clan elders were about to offer water chestnuts, but Qu Jian ordered them removed, saying, 'The sacrificial canon has this: the ruler of a state has the ox offering, a great officer has the sheep presentation, a knight has the libation of pig and dog, common people have offerings of fish and roast meat, and with baskets and dishes of dried meat and mince, high and low are settled.
translations.idiomatic: After Qu Dao died, the elders prepared water chestnuts, but Qu Jian had them removed, explaining that the ritual canon assigns oxen, sheep, pigs and dogs, fish and roasted meat, baskets, and dishes according to rank.

sentences.zh: 不羞珍異，不陳庶侈，不以私欲幹國之典』遂不用。」

translations.literal: It does not present rare and strange things, does not set out common extravagances, and does not use private desire to interfere with the state canon'; accordingly they did not use them."
translations.idiomatic: It does not present exotic delicacies or private extravagance, and it does not let personal desire disturb the state ritual. So the water chestnuts were not used."

sentences.zh: 此則禮外之食，前賢不敢薦也。

translations.literal: This means that foods outside ritual were things earlier worthies did not dare to offer.
translations.idiomatic: Thus earlier worthies would not offer foods outside the ritual code.

sentences.zh: 今欲取甘旨之物，肥濃之味，隨所有者皆充祭用，苟逾舊制，其何限焉。

translations.literal: Now if one wishes to take sweet and savory things, rich and heavy flavors, and, according to whatever exists, fill out sacrificial use with all of them, then exceeding the old system would leave no limit.
translations.idiomatic: If every sweet, rich, or savory food at hand is admitted into sacrifice, then once the old rules are exceeded there will be no limit.

sentences.zh: 雖籩豆有加，豈能備也？

translations.literal: Even if baskets and dishes are increased, how could they be complete?
translations.idiomatic: Even adding more baskets and dishes, how could the offerings ever be exhaustive?

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「大羹不致，粢食不鑿，昭其儉也。」

translations.literal: 《Tradition》 says: "The great soup is not richly seasoned, and the grain food is not finely polished, displaying frugality."
translations.idiomatic: 《Tradition》 says: "The great soup is not richly seasoned, and the grain food is not finely polished, displaying frugality."

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。」

translations.literal: 《Documents》 says: "Millet and panicled millet are not the fragrance; bright virtue alone is fragrant."
translations.idiomatic: 《Documents》 says: "Millet and panicled millet are not the fragrance; bright virtue alone is fragrant."

sentences.zh: 事神在於虔誠，不求厭飫。

translations.literal: Serving spirits lies in reverent sincerity, not in seeking satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the spirits depends on sincerity, not on feeding them to fullness.

sentences.zh: 三年一禘，不欲黷也。

translations.literal: The di sacrifice occurs once in three years because one does not wish to make it profane by frequency.
translations.idiomatic: The di sacrifice is held only once every three years to avoid irreverent overuse.

sentences.zh: 三獻而終，禮有成也。

translations.literal: It ends after the three offerings because ritual has completion.
translations.idiomatic: The rite ends with three offerings because ritual must have a proper completion.

sentences.zh: 《風》有《采蘋》、《采蘩》，《雅》有《行葦》《泂酌》，守以忠信，神其舍諸！

translations.literal: In the 《Airs》 there are 《Gathering Duckweed》 and 《Gathering Artemisia》; in the 《Ya》 there are 《Walking Among the Reeds》 and 《Clear Libation》. If they are kept with loyalty and trust, would the spirits reject them!
translations.idiomatic: The 《Airs》 have 《Gathering Duckweed》 and 《Gathering Artemisia》; the 《Ya》 has 《Walking Among the Reeds》 and 《Clear Libation》. If offerings are kept with loyalty and trust, surely the spirits would not reject them!

sentences.zh: 若以今之珍饌，平生所習，求神無方，何必師古。

translations.literal: If one uses today's precious foods, what one was accustomed to in ordinary life, seeking the spirits without method, there would be no need to take antiquity as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: If current delicacies and everyday habits are enough to seek the spirits, then there is no reason to follow antiquity at all.

sentences.zh: 簠簋可去，而盤盂杯案當在御矣。

translations.literal: The fu and gui vessels could be discarded, and plates, bowls, cups, and trays ought to be used instead.
translations.idiomatic: On that logic, ritual vessels could be thrown out and replaced with plates, bowls, cups, and trays.

sentences.zh: 《韶》《頀》可息，而箜篌笛笙當在奏矣。

translations.literal: 《Shao》 and 《Hu》 could be stopped, and harps, flutes, and mouth organs ought to be performed instead.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient music 《Shao》 and 《Hu》 could likewise give way to harps, flutes, and pipes.

sentences.zh: 凡斯之流，皆非正物，或興於近代，或出於蕃夷，耳目之娛，本無則象，用之宗廟，後嗣何觀？

translations.literal: All things of this sort are not proper objects. Some arose in recent times, some came from foreign peoples. Pleasures of the ears and eyes originally have no model. If used in the ancestral temple, what will later descendants observe?
translations.idiomatic: Such things are not proper ritual objects. Some are recent innovations, others foreign imports, and pleasures for eye and ear have no ritual model; if used in the ancestral temple, what would descendants see?

sentences.zh: 欲為永式，恐未可也。

translations.literal: If one wishes to make them a permanent rule, I fear it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: They should not be made a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 且自漢已降，諸陵皆有寢宮，歲時朔望，薦以常饌，此既常行，亦足盡至孝之情矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, from the Han onward, all tombs have had resting palaces. At seasonal times and on new and full moons, ordinary foods are offered there. Since this is already regularly practiced, it is enough to exhaust the feeling of utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Han, mausoleums have had halls where ordinary foods are offered seasonally and on new and full moons; this already satisfies the deepest filial feeling.

sentences.zh: 宗廟正禮，宜仍典故，率情變革，人情所難。

translations.literal: For the correct rites of the ancestral temple, one should follow the precedents. To follow feeling and change them is difficult for human sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: The formal rites of the ancestral temple should follow precedent; changing them by emotion is hard to justify.

sentences.zh: 又按舊制，一升曰爵，五升曰散。

translations.literal: Again, according to the old system, one sheng is called a jue, and five sheng are called a san.
translations.idiomatic: The old system called a one-sheng vessel a jue and a five-sheng vessel a san.

sentences.zh: 《禮器》稱：「宗廟之祭，貴者獻以爵，賤者獻以散。」

translations.literal: 《Ritual Vessels》 says: "In ancestral-temple sacrifices, the honored offer with the jue, and the lowly offer with the san."
translations.idiomatic: 《Ritual Vessels》 says: "In ancestral-temple sacrifices, the honored offer with the jue, and the lowly offer with the san."

sentences.zh: 此明貴小賤大，示之節儉。

translations.literal: This makes clear that the honored use the small and the lowly use the large, showing frugality.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that high rank is marked by smaller vessels, a lesson in restraint.

sentences.zh: 又按《國語》觀射父曰：「郊禘不過繭栗，蒸嘗不過把握。」

translations.literal: Again, according to 《Guoyu》, Guan Shefu said: "For the jiao and di sacrifices, they do not exceed cocoon and chestnut size; for zheng and chang sacrifices, they do not exceed what can be grasped."
translations.idiomatic: 《Guoyu》 has Guan Shefu say: "The jiao and di sacrifices do not exceed cocoon and chestnut size; the zheng and chang sacrifices do not exceed what can be grasped."

sentences.zh: 夫神，以精明臨人者也，所求備物，不求豐大。

translations.literal: Spirits come before people with pure brightness; what they seek is complete objects, not abundance and size.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits attend in pure clarity; they require the prescribed set of offerings, not lavish quantity or size.

sentences.zh: 苟失於禮，雖多何為？

translations.literal: If one loses ritual, even if there is much, what use is it?
translations.idiomatic: If ritual is lost, what use is abundance?

sentences.zh: 豈可舍先王之遺法，徇一時之所尚，廢棄禮經，以從流欲。

translations.literal: One must not abandon the bequeathed laws of the former kings, follow what is fashionable for a moment, discard the ritual classics, and follow drifting desires.
translations.idiomatic: One cannot abandon the former kings' rules, chase the fashion of the moment, and cast aside the ritual classics for passing desire.

sentences.zh: 裂冠毀冕，將安用之！

translations.literal: If caps are torn and crowns destroyed, what use will they be!
translations.idiomatic: What use is a cap torn apart and a crown destroyed!

sentences.zh: 且君子愛人以禮，不求苟合，況在宗廟，敢忘舊章。

translations.literal: Moreover, the gentleman loves people by means of ritual and does not seek careless conformity; still less, in the ancestral temple, would he dare forget the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman cares for others through ritual and does not seek easy compliance; in the ancestral temple, he certainly cannot forget the old rules.

sentences.zh: 請依古制，庶可經久。

translations.literal: We request that the ancient system be followed; perhaps it can endure for long.
translations.idiomatic: We request adherence to the ancient system, so the practice may endure.

sentences.zh: 禮部員外郎楊仲昌議曰：「謹按《禮》曰：『夫祭不欲煩，煩則黷；

translations.literal: Vice Director of Rites Yang Zhongchang argued: "Respectfully according to the 《Rites》: 'Sacrifice should not be troublesome--if troublesome it becomes irreverent;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of Rites Yang Zhongchang argued: "Respectfully according to the 《Rites》: 'Sacrifice should not be troublesome--if troublesome it becomes irreverent;

sentences.zh: 亦不欲簡，簡則怠。』

translations.literal: nor should it be too simple—if too simple it becomes negligent.
translations.idiomatic: Nor should it be too simple; if too simple, it becomes negligent.'

sentences.zh: 又鄭玄云：『人生尚褻食，鬼神則不然。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan also said: 'While the living esteem coarse food, spirits are not so.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan also said: 'While the living esteem coarse food, spirits are not so.

sentences.zh: 神農時雖有黍稷，猶未有酒醴。

translations.literal: In the time of Shennong there were millet and panic grass but still no wine or ale.
translations.idiomatic: In Shennong’s age there was grain but no wine.

sentences.zh: 及後聖作為醴酪，猶存玄酒，求不忘古。』

translations.literal: When later sages made ale and cheese, they still kept the dark liquor, seeking not to forget antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: When later sages made ale and cheese, they still kept the dark liquor, seeking not to forget antiquity.'

sentences.zh: 《春秋》曰：『蘋蘩、蘊藻之菜，潢汙行潦之水，可羞于王公，可薦於鬼神。』

translations.literal: The 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 says: 'Water-cress and pondweed, water from puddles and roadside ditches, may be set before kings and dukes and offered to spirits.'
translations.idiomatic: The 《Annals》 say pondweed and ditch water may honor kings and spirits.

sentences.zh: 又曰：『大羹不和，粢食不鑿。』

translations.literal: It also says: 'Great broth unseasoned, millet food unpolished.'
translations.idiomatic: It also says great broth is unseasoned and millet left unpolished.

sentences.zh: 此明君人者，有國奉先，敬神嚴享，豈肥濃以為尚，將儉約以表誠。

translations.literal: This shows that rulers with a state who serve their ancestors and revere spirits in solemn offering do not take richness and heaviness as the standard but use frugality to show sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers honor ancestors by frugality, not by rich food.

sentences.zh: 則陸海之物，鮮肥之類，既乖禮文之情，而變作者之法，皆充祭用，非所詳也。

translations.literal: Then goods from land and sea and fresh, fatty kinds, being contrary to ritual sentiment and to the law of offerings, if all were used in sacrifice, are not to be approved.
translations.idiomatic: Sea and land delicacies violate ritual and should not all enter sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『樽酒簋貳，用缶，納約自牖。』

translations.literal: The 《Changes》 says: 'One wine vessel, two gui of grain, using an earthenware jar, presenting the offering through the window.'
translations.idiomatic: The 《Changes》 prescribe one wine vessel and two gui in an earthen jar.

sentences.zh: 此明祭存簡易，不在繁奢。

translations.literal: This shows sacrifice keeps to simplicity and lies not in multiplicity and luxury.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice should be simple, not lavish.

sentences.zh: 所以一樽之酒，貳簋之奠，為明祀也。

translations.literal: Therefore one vessel of wine and two gui of offering make the meaning of sacrifice clear.
translations.idiomatic: One wine and two gui suffice for clear sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 抑又聞之，夫義以出禮，禮以體政，違則有紊，是稱不經。

translations.literal: Moreover it is heard that righteousness produces ritual and ritual embodies government; to violate it is disorder—this is called uncanonical.
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness begets ritual; ritual embodies government—violation is disorder.

sentences.zh: 薦肥濃則褻味有登，加籩爵則事非師古。

translations.literal: To offer rich and heavy flavors is to set coarse tastes on high; to add baskets and cups is to depart from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Rich offerings vulgarize taste; added baskets and cups abandon antiquity.

sentences.zh: 與其別行新制，寧如謹守舊章？」

translations.literal: Rather than separately put a new regulation into effect, would it not be better to respectfully keep the old statutes?"
translations.idiomatic: Rather than separately put a new regulation into effect, would it not be better to respectfully keep the old statutes?"

sentences.zh: 時太子賓客崔沔、戶部郎中楊伯成、左衛兵曹劉秩等皆建議以為請依舊禮，不可改易。

translations.literal: At the time Crown Prince Guest Cui Mian, Bureau Director Yang Bocheng, Left Guard Army Cao Liu Zhi, and others all argued to follow the old rites and not change them.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Mian, Yang Bocheng, Liu Zhi, and others all urged keeping the old rites.

sentences.zh: 於是宰臣等具沔、述等議以奏。

translations.literal: Thereupon the chief ministers presented the recommendations of Mian, Shu, and the rest for memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers submitted Mian’s and Shu’s views.

sentences.zh: 玄宗曰：「朕承祖宗休德，至於享祀粢盛，實思豐潔，禮物之具，諒在昭忠。

translations.literal: Xuanzong said: "We inherit the fine virtue of Our ancestors; as for the grain offerings in sacrifice, We truly wish them abundant and pure, and the equipment of ritual objects should show loyal reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong said: "We inherit our ancestors' virtue and want the sacrificial grain offerings abundant and pure, with ritual vessels showing loyal reverence.

sentences.zh: 其非芳潔不應法制者，亦不可用。」

translations.literal: Those that are not fragrant and pure, or that do not accord with the regulations, also may not be used."
translations.idiomatic: Anything impure or uncanonical may not be used."

sentences.zh: 以是更令太常量加品味。

translations.literal: For this reason, he further ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to add varieties of flavors in measured amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered the Court of Sacrifices to add varieties of offerings in measured amounts.

sentences.zh: 韋縚又奏：「請每室加籩、豆各六，每四時異品，以當時新果及珍羞同薦。」

translations.literal: Wei Tao again memorialized: "I request adding six baskets and six bean-vessels to each chamber; in each of the four seasons, different items should be offered, with fresh fruits of the time and rare delicacies presented together."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Tao asked: "Add six more baskets and bean-vessels per chamber, with seasonal fruit and delicacies."

sentences.zh: 則可之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 又酌獻酒爵，玄宗令用龠升一升，合于古義，而多少適中。

translations.literal: As to the libation cups, Xuanzong ordered the use of the yue sheng of one sheng, in accord with ancient meaning and moderate in amount.
translations.idiomatic: Libation cups were set at one sheng by the yue measure—ancient and moderate.

sentences.zh: 自是常依行焉。

translations.literal: From then on this was regularly followed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter this practice stood.

sentences.zh: 後漢世祖光武皇帝葬于原陵，其子孝明帝追思不已，

translations.literal: Later Han Emperor Guangwu was buried at Yuanling; his son Emperor Ming never ceased to mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu of Later Han was buried at Yuanling; his son Emperor Ming long mourned him.

sentences.zh: 永平元年，乃率諸侯王、公卿，正月朝于原陵，親奉先后陰氏妝奩篋笥悲慟，左右侍臣，莫不嗚咽。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongping, he then led the feudal princes and kings, dukes, and ministers to attend Yuanling in the first month; personally presenting the dressing cases and boxes of the late Empress Yin, he grieved bitterly, and the attendants at his side all sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping 1: Emperor Ming led princes and ministers to Yuanling in the first month, grieving over Empress Yin's toilet goods while attendants sobbed.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝父丹陽尹順之，追尊為太祖文帝，先葬丹徒，亦尊為建陵。

translations.literal: Liang Wudi’s father, Director of Danyang Shunzhi, was posthumously honored as Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen and was first buried at Dantu; he was also honored as Jianling.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wudi’s father Shunzhi, made Grand Ancestor Wen, lay at Dantu and Jianling.

sentences.zh: 武帝即大位後，大同十五年，亦朝於建陵，有紫雲廕覆陵上，食頃方滅。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu took the throne, in the fifteenth year of Datong, he also attended Jianling; purple clouds shaded and covered the mound, dispersing only after the time it takes to eat a meal.
translations.idiomatic: After Wudi's accession, Datong 15, he visited Jianling; purple clouds covered the mound briefly.

sentences.zh: 梁主著單衣介幘，設次而拜，望陵流哭，淚之所沾，草皆變色。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler wore a single garment and a kerchief, set up a tent and bowed, gazed at the mound and wept streaming tears; where the tears fell, the grass changed color.
translations.idiomatic: He wore plain dress, bowed at a tent, wept until the grass changed color where tears fell.

sentences.zh: 陵傍有枯泉，至時而水流香潔。

translations.literal: Beside the mound was a dry spring that at the time flowed fragrant and clear.
translations.idiomatic: A dry spring beside the tomb briefly flowed sweet and clear.

sentences.zh: 因謂侍臣曰：「陵陰石虎，與陵俱創二百餘年，恨小，可更造碑石柱麟，並二陵中道門為三闥。

translations.literal: He therefore told his attendants: "The stone tigers by the mound were made with the mound more than two hundred years ago; regretting their small size, they may be remade as steles, stone pillars, and qilin, and the middle gate of the two mounds made into three gates.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore told his attendants: "The stone tigers by the mound were made with the mound more than two hundred years ago; regretting their small size, they may be remade as steles, stone pillars, and qilin, and the middle gate of the two mounds made into three gates.

sentences.zh: 園陵職司，並賜一級。」

translations.literal: The staff of the park and tombs were all promoted one rank."
translations.idiomatic: The staff of the park and tombs were all promoted one rank."

sentences.zh: 奉辭諸陵，哭踴而拜。

translations.literal: Having paid respects at the various mounds, he wept and bowed in the full mourning leap.
translations.idiomatic: He took leave of each tomb with weeping and the mourning leap.

sentences.zh: 周太祖文帝葬于成陵，其子明帝初立，元年十二月，謁於成陵。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou Grand Ancestor Wen was buried at Chengling; his son Emperor Ming, on first accession, in the twelfth month of the first year, visited Chengling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Grand Ancestor Wen lay at Chengling; Ming visited in the twelfth month of his first year.

sentences.zh: 高祖神堯葬於獻陵，貞觀十三年正月乙巳，太宗朝於獻陵。

translations.literal: Gaozu Shenyao was buried at Xianling; on the yisi day of the first month of the thirteenth year of Zhenguan, Taizong attended Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu lay at Xianling; Zhenguan 13, first month, yisi day, Taizong visited the mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 先是日，宿衛設黃麾仗周衛陵寢，至是質明，七廟子孫及諸侯百僚、蕃夷君長皆陪列于司馬門內。

translations.literal: On the day before, the guard set yellow awnings and surrounded the tomb precinct; at daybreak the descendants of the seven temples, the feudal lords, the hundred officials, and tribal chieftains all stood in ranks inside the Sima Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, guards ringed the tomb; at dawn imperial kin, nobles, officials, and chieftains lined the Sima Gate.

sentences.zh: 皇帝至小次，降輿納履，哭于闕門，西面再拜，慟絕不能興。

translations.literal: The emperor reached the small shelter, descended the carriage, put on shoes, wept at the gate tower facing west and bowed twice, and was overcome and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept twice west of the gate tower and could not rise.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，改服入于寢宮，親執饌，閱視高祖及先后服御之物，匍匐床前悲慟。

translations.literal: When the rites were done, he changed dress and entered the sleeping palace, personally held the food trays, and inspected the garments and goods of Gaozu and the late empress, crawling before the bed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the sleeping palace, inspected Gaozu’s and the empress’s goods, and wept before the bed.

sentences.zh: 左右侍御者莫不歔欷。

translations.literal: Those attending at left and right all sighed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants all wept.

sentences.zh: 初，甲辰之夜，大雨雪。

translations.literal: Earlier, on the night of jiachen, great rain and snow had fallen.
translations.idiomatic: The night before jiachen brought heavy snow.

sentences.zh: 及皇帝入陵院，悲號哽咽，百辟哀慟，是時雪益甚，寒風暴起，有蒼雲出於山陵之上，俄而流布，天地晦冥。

translations.literal: When the emperor entered the tomb precinct, wailing and sobbing, the hundred ministers grieved; at that time the snow increased, a cold wind rose violently, and dark clouds issued from above the hill-tomb, soon spreading; heaven and earth were dim.
translations.idiomatic: As he entered the precinct all wailed; snow thickened, wind rose, dark clouds spread from the mound.

sentences.zh: 至禮畢，皇帝出自寢宮，步過司馬門北，泥行二百餘步，於是風靜雪止，雲氣歇滅，天色開霽。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished and the emperor came out from the sleeping palace, he walked north past the Sima Gate, treading mud for more than two hundred paces; then the wind stilled, the snow stopped, the clouds dispersed, and the sky cleared.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites he walked two hundred paces in mud north of the Sima Gate; then wind and snow ceased and the sky cleared.

sentences.zh: 觀者竊議，以為孝感之所致焉。

translations.literal: Onlookers privately said it was brought about by filial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers called it filial piety moving heaven.

sentences.zh: 是日曲赦三原縣及從官衛士等，大辟已下，已發覺，未發覺，皆釋其罪。

translations.literal: That day a partial amnesty was granted to Sanyuan County and the attendant guards and officers; for capital crimes and below, whether discovered or not, all were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: That day Sanyuan and the guard received partial amnesty through capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 免民一年租賦。

translations.literal: The people’s one-year land tax and corvée were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: A year’s land tax was remitted.

sentences.zh: 有八十已上，及孝子順孫、義夫節婦、鰥寡孤獨、有篤疾者，賜物各有差。

translations.literal: Those eighty and above, filial sons and compliant grandsons, righteous husbands and chaste wives, widowers, orphans, and solitaries, and those with grave illness received gifts in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The aged, the filial, the chaste, widows, orphans, and the gravely ill received graded gifts.

sentences.zh: 宿衛陵邑中郎將、衛士齋員及三原令以下，各賜爵一級。

translations.literal: The Central Guard lieutenant of the tomb district, fast-day guards, and all from the magistrate of Sanyuan downward each received promotion of one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb guards and officials through the magistrate of Sanyuan gained one rank.

sentences.zh: 丁未，至自獻陵。

translations.literal: On dingwei, he returned from Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he returned from Xianling.

sentences.zh: 己酉，朝於太極殿。

translations.literal: On jiyou, he attended court at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou he held court at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 庚子，會群臣，奏《功成慶善》及《破陣》之樂。

translations.literal: On gengzi, he gathered the ministers and presented the music 《Achievement Complete, Celebration of Good》 and 《Breaking the Battle Line》.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he had ministers hear 《Achievement Complete》 and 《Breaking the Battle Line》.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元十七年十一月丙申，親謁橋陵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the bingshen day, of the seventeenth year of Xuanzong's Kaiyuan era, he personally visited Qiaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 17, eleventh month, bingshen day: Xuanzong visited Qiaoling.

sentences.zh: 皇帝望陵涕泣，左右並哀感。

translations.literal: Gazing at the mound, the emperor wept; those at his left and right were all moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: He wept at the mound; attendants grieved with him.

sentences.zh: 進奉先縣同赤縣，以所管萬三百戶供陵寢，三府兵馬供衛，曲赦縣內大辟罪已下。

translations.literal: Fengxian County was advanced to the status of a red county; its 103,000 households were assigned to supply the tomb, and troops of the three metropolitan prefectures to guard; a partial amnesty within the county for crimes below capital grade.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian became a red county; 103,000 households supplied the tomb; three prefectures guarded; the county was partially amnestied.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，謁定陵。

translations.literal: On wuxu, he visited Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu he visited Dingling.

sentences.zh: 己亥，謁獻陵。

translations.literal: On jihai, he visited Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he visited Xianling.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，謁昭陵。

translations.literal: On renyin, he visited Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he visited Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 己巳，謁乾陵。

translations.literal: On jisi, he visited Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he visited Qianling.

sentences.zh: 戊申，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On wushen, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下，流移人並放還，左降官移近處，百姓無出今年地稅之半。

translations.literal: A great amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm; displaced persons were all sent home; demoted officials were moved nearer; the people paid no more than half this year’s land tax.
translations.idiomatic: He amnestied the realm, sent exiles home, moved demoted officials nearer, and halved the land tax.

sentences.zh: 每陵取側近六鄉以供陵寢。

translations.literal: For each tomb, six neighboring townships were taken to supply the tomb precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Six townships near each tomb supplied the mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 皇帝初至橋陵，質明，柏樹甘露降，曙後祥煙遍空。

translations.literal: When the emperor first reached Qiaoling, at daybreak sweet dew fell on the cypress trees; after dawn auspicious mist filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: At Qiaoling dawn brought dew on cypresses and auspicious mist after sunrise.

sentences.zh: 皇帝謁昭陵，陪葬功臣盡來受饗，鳳吹釭釭，若神祇之所集。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Zhaoling, the meritorious ministers buried with him all came to receive offerings; phoenix music rang clearly as if spirits were gathered.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhaoling companion ministers received offerings; phoenix music rang as if spirits gathered.

sentences.zh: 陪位文武百僚皆聞先聖歎息、功臣蹈舞之聲，皆以為至孝所感。

translations.literal: The civil and military officials in attendance all heard the sighs of the former sage and the treading dance of the meritorious ministers, and all took it as a response to utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Attending officials heard sighs and dancing—they called it utmost filial piety.

sentences.zh: 天寶二年八月，制：「自今已後，每至九月一日，薦衣於陵寢。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Tianbao, an edict said: "From now on, whenever the first day of the ninth month arrives, garments shall be offered at the tomb halls."
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao 2, eighth month: an edict ordered, "Offer garments at the tomb halls every ninth month, first day."

sentences.zh: 十三載，改獻、昭、乾、定、橋五陵署為臺，其署令改為臺令，加舊一級。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the five mausoleum offices of Xian, Zhao, Qian, Ding, and Qiao were changed into directorates; their office directors were changed into directorate directors, one grade above the old rank.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13, the five mausoleum offices became directorates, and their chiefs gained one rank.
